"First Moon landing" and "The Moon landing" redirect here. For other crewed or uncrewed
Moon landings, see [Moon landing](#Lunar_surface_operations "Contents").

This article is about the 1969 crewed lunar mission. For other uses, see [Apollo 11 (disambiguation)](#Return "Contents").

**Apollo 11** (July 16–24, 1969) was the American [spaceflight](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") that first landed [humans](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") on the [Moon](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), and the fifth [crewed mission](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") of [NASA](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options")'s [Apollo program](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options"). The mission was crewed by Commander [Neil Armstrong](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu"), Command Module Pilot [Michael Collins](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu"), and Lunar Module Pilot [Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu"), all of whom were on their second and final spaceflight.

Launched atop a [Saturn V](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") rocket from [Kennedy Space Center](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") in [Florida](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") on July 16 at 13:32 [UTC](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title="), the Apollo spacecraft consisted of three parts: the [command module](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") (CM), which housed the three astronauts and was the only part to return to Earth; the [service module](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") (SM), which provided propulsion, electrical power, oxygen, and water to the command module; and the [Lunar Module](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") (LM), which had two stages—a descent stage with a large engine and fuel tanks for landing on the Moon, and a lighter ascent stage containing a cabin for two astronauts and a small engine to return them to [lunar orbit](# "Contents"). After a three-day transit, Armstrong and Aldrin descended to the surface aboard the LM *[Eagle](#
"Contents")*, landing in the Sea of Tranquility ([Mare Tranquillitatis](# "Contents")) on July 20 at 20:17 UTC while Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard the CM *[Columbia](#
"Contents")*. Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon approximately
six hours after landing, followed by Aldrin nineteen minutes later. Together they
spent around two and a half hours walking on the surface, planting an [American flag](# "Contents"), speaking with President [Richard Nixon](# "Contents") who was in the [White House](# "Contents"), deploying scientific instruments, and collecting
21.5 kg (47.5 lb) of lunar material. After more than 21 hours on the surface,
they rejoined Collins in lunar orbit, and the crew returned safely to [Earth](# "Contents") on July 24, splashing down in the [Pacific Ocean](# "Contents").

Apollo 11 was the culmination of the [Space Race](#Background "Contents"), a geopolitical competition between the United States and the [Soviet Union](#Personnel "Contents") rooted in [Cold War](#Personnel "Contents") rivalry. It fulfilled a national goal set by President [John F. Kennedy](#Prime_crew "Contents") in May 1961, who had [challenged](#Prime_crew "Contents") the United States to land a man on the Moon and return him safely before the end of the decade. The program overcame a severe setback with the fatal [Apollo 1](#Prime_crew "Contents") launchpad fire in January 1967 and drew on technologies developed through the preceding [Mercury](#Backup_crew "Contents") and [Gemini](#Backup_crew "Contents") programs. The Soviet Union, despite early leads in spaceflight, was unable to match the Saturn V rocket, and its uncrewed lunar probe [Luna 15](#Support_crew "Contents") crashed on the Moon on July 21, while Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin were still on the lunar surface.

Armstrong's moonwalk was broadcast live to an estimated 600 million viewers, roughly
one-fifth of the world's population, making it among the most-watched [television](#Capsule_communicators "Contents") events in history. Stepping onto the lunar surface, Armstrong declared: "[That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind](#Flight_directors "Contents")." [Lunar samples](#Flight_directors "Contents") returned by the mission led to the identification of three previously unrecognized minerals, and scientific instruments deployed on the surface continued returning data for years afterwards. The crew were honoured with [ticker-tape parades](#Other_key_personnel "Contents"), a world goodwill tour, and the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](#Preparations "Contents"). The command module
*Columbia* is preserved at the [National Air and Space Museum](#Preparations "Contents") in [Washington, D.C.](#Insignia "Contents"), while the descent stage of
*Eagle* remains on the lunar surface.


## Background

In the late 1950s and early 1960s, the United States was engaged in the [Cold War](#Call_signs "Contents"), a geopolitical rivalry with the [Soviet Union](#Call_signs
"Contents").[[14]](#First-step_decision "Contents") On October 4, 1957, the Soviet
Union launched *[Sputnik 1](#First-step_decision "Contents")*, the first [artificial satellite](#Pre-launch "Contents"), surprising the world and fueling fears about Soviet technological and military capabilities. Its success demonstrated that the USSR could potentially deliver [nuclear weapons](#Pre-launch "Contents") over [intercontinental distances](#Mission "Contents"), challenging American claims of military, economic, and technological
superiority.[[15]](#Lunar_descent "Contents")

This incident sparked the [Sputnik crisis](#Landing "Contents") and ignited the [Space Race](#Landing "Contents"), as both superpowers sought to demonstrate superiority in
spaceflight.[[16]](#Columbia_in_lunar_orbit "Contents") President [Dwight D. Eisenhower](#Return "Contents") responded to the challenge posed by Sputnik by creating the [National Aeronautics and Space Administration](#Return "Contents") (NASA), and initiating [Project Mercury](#Splashdown_and_quarantine
"Contents"),[[17]](#World_tour "Contents") which aimed to place a man into [Earth orbit](#World_tour
"Contents").[[18]](#Spacecraft "Contents") The Soviets took the lead on April 12,
1961, when [cosmonaut](#Spacecraft "Contents") [Yuri Gagarin](#Moon_rocks "Contents") became the first person in space and the first to orbit the
Earth.[[19]](#Lunar_Module_Eagle_memorabilia "Contents") Nearly a month later, on
May 5, 1961, Alan Shepard became the first American in space; his 15-minute flight
was suborbital, not a full orbit.[[20]](#50th_anniversary "Contents")

Because the Soviet Union had [launch vehicles](#Films_and_documentaries "Contents") with higher lift capacity, President John F. Kennedy, Eisenhower's successor, chose a challenge that exceeded the capabilities of the existing generation of rockets, so that both countries would be starting from an equal position. A crewed mission to the Moon would serve this
purpose.[[21]](#Notes "Contents")

On May 25, 1961, Kennedy addressed the [United States Congress](#Notes "Contents") on "Urgent National Needs" and declared:

> I believe that this nation should commit itself to achieving the goal, before this
decade [1960s] is out, of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to the
Earth. No single space project in this period will be more impressive to mankind,
or more important for the long-range exploration of space; and none will be so difficult
or expensive to accomplish. We propose to accelerate the development of the appropriate
lunar space craft. We propose to develop alternate liquid and solid fuel boosters,
much larger than any now being developed, until certain which is superior. We propose
additional funds for other engine development and for unmanned explorations—explorations
which are particularly important for one purpose which this nation will never overlook:
the survival of the man who first makes this daring flight. But in a very real sense,
it will not be one man going to the Moon—if we make this judgment affirmatively,
it will be an entire nation. For all of us must work to put him there.


— Kennedy's speech to Congress[[22]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans")

On September 12, 1962, Kennedy [delivered another speech](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans") before a crowd of about 40,000 people in the [Rice University football stadium](af "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans") in [Houston](https://am.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%8A%A0%E1%8D%96%E1%88%8E_%E1%8D%B2%E1%8D%A9 "አፖሎ ፲፩ – Amharic"),
Texas.[[23]](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Aragonese")[[24]](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88_11 "أبولو 11 – Arabic")
A widely quoted refrain from the middle portion of the speech reads as follows:

> There is no strife, no prejudice, no national conflict in outer space as yet. Its
hazards are hostile to us all. Its conquest deserves the best of all mankind, and
its opportunity for peaceful cooperation may never come again. But why, some say,
the Moon? Why choose this as our goal? And they may well ask, why climb the highest
mountain? Why, 35 years ago, [fly the Atlantic](https://be.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD-11 "Апалон-11 – Belarusian")? Why does [Rice play Texas](https://be.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD-11 "Апалон-11 – Belarusian")?
> We choose to go to the Moon! We choose to go to the Moon ... We choose to
go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things, not because they are easy,
but because they are hard; because that goal will serve to organize and measure the
best of our energies and skills, because that challenge is one that we are willing
to accept, one we are unwilling to postpone, and one we intend to win, and the others,
too.[[25]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%85%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8B_%E0%A7%A7%E0%A7%A7 "অ্যাপোলো ১১ – Bangla")
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Apollo 11 – Breton")](https://br.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Breton")
President [John F. Kennedy](https://ceb.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_XI "Apollo XI – Cebuano") [speaking at Rice University](https://ckb.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A6%DB%95%D9%BE%DB%86%D9%84%DB%86_%D9%A1%D9%A1 "ئەپۆلۆ ١١ – Central Kurdish") on September 12, 1962
In spite of that, the proposed program faced widespread opposition and was dubbed
a "[moondoggle](ckb "ئەپۆلۆ ١١")" by [Norbert Wiener](https://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article"), a mathematician at the [Massachusetts Institute of Technology](https://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good
article").[[26]](cv "Аполлон-11 – Chuvash")[[27]](https://da.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Danish")
The effort to land a man on the Moon already had a name: [Project Apollo](da "Apollo 11 –
Danish").[[28]](eo "Apollo 11 – Esperanto") When Kennedy met with [Nikita Khrushchev](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apolo_11 "featured article"), the [Premier of the Soviet Union](es "Apolo 11") in June 1961, he proposed making the Moon landing a joint project, but Khrushchev declined the
offer.[[29]](fa "آپولو ۱۱") Kennedy again proposed a joint expedition to
the Moon in a speech to the [United Nations General Assembly](fi "Apollo 11 – Finnish") on September 20,
1963.[[30]](https://fy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article") The idea of
a joint Moon mission was ultimately abandoned after Kennedy's death.[[31]](https://ga.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Irish")

An early and crucial decision was choosing [lunar orbit rendezvous](https://gl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Galician") over both [direct ascent](gl "Apollo 11") and [Earth orbit rendezvous](https://gu.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%AA%8F%E0%AA%AA%E0%AB%8B%E0%AA%B2%E0%AB%8B_%E0%AB%A7%E0%AB%A7 "એપોલો ૧૧ – Gujarati"). A [space rendezvous](gu "એપોલો ૧૧ – Gujarati") is an [orbital maneuver](https://gv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Manx") in which two spacecraft navigate through space and meet up. In July 1962, NASA head [James Webb](https://gv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Manx") announced that lunar orbit rendezvous would be
used[[32]](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%90%D7%A4%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%95_11 "Apollo 11")[[33]](https://hu.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo%E2%80%9311 "Apollo 11")
and that the [Apollo spacecraft](https://hu.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo%E2%80%9311 "featured article") would have three major parts: a command module (CM) with a cabin for the three astronauts, and the only part that returned to Earth; a service module (SM), which supported the command module with propulsion, electrical power, oxygen, and water; and a lunar module (LM) that had two stages—a descent stage for landing on the Moon, and an ascent stage to place the astronauts back into lunar
orbit.[[34]](is "Tungllendingin (1969) – Icelandic") This design meant the spacecraft
could be launched by a single [Saturn V](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article") rocket that was then under
development.[[35]](https://ka.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%83%90%E1%83%9E%E1%83%9D%E1%83%9A%E1%83%9D_11 "აპოლო 11 – Georgian")

Technologies and techniques required for Apollo were developed by [Project Gemini](https://kk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD_11 "Аполлон 11 –
Kazakh").[[36]](https://ks.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A7%D9%BE%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88_%DB%B1%DB%B1 "اپولو ۱۱ – Kashmiri")
The Apollo project was enabled by NASA's adoption of new advances in [semiconductor device](ks "اپولو ۱۱"), including [metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors](https://ku.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Kurdish") (MOSFETs) in the [Interplanetary Monitoring Platform](https://la.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latin")
(IMP)[[37]](lmo "Apollo XI – Lombard")[[38]](https://lv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latvian")
and [silicon](https://lv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latvian") [integrated circuit](https://mg.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11") (IC) chips in the [Apollo Guidance Computer](https://mg.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Malagasy")
(AGC).[[39]](min "Apollo 11 – Minangkabau")

Project Apollo was abruptly halted by the [Apollo 1](https://mk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 – Macedonian") fire on January 27, 1967, in which astronauts [Gus Grissom](mk "Аполо 11"), [Ed White](https://ml.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%B4%85%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8D%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8B%E0%B4%B3%E0%B5%8B_11 "അപ്പോളോ 11 – Malayalam"), and [Roger B. Chaffee](https://ml.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%B4%85%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8D%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8B%E0%B4%B3%E0%B5%8B_11 "അപ്പോളോ 11 – Malayalam") died, and the subsequent
investigation.[[40]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")
In October 1968, [Apollo 7](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") evaluated the command module in Earth
orbit,[[41]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
and in December [Apollo 8](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") tested it in lunar
orbit.[[42]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
In March 1969, [Apollo 9](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") put the lunar module through its paces in Earth
orbit,[[43]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
and in May [Apollo 10](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") conducted a "dress rehearsal" in lunar orbit. By July 1969, all was in readiness for Apollo 11 to take the final step onto the
Moon.[[44]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

The Soviet Union appeared to be winning the Space Race, but its early lead was overtaken
by the US [Gemini program](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") and Soviet failure to develop the [N1 launcher](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), which would have been comparable to the Saturn
V.[[45]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Seeing these failures, the Soviets then attempted to beat the US to return lunar
material to the Earth by means of [uncrewed probes](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"). On July 13, three days before Apollo 11's launch, the Soviet Union launched [Luna 15](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), which reached lunar orbit before Apollo 11. During descent, a malfunction caused Luna 15 to crash in [Mare Crisium](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") about two hours before Armstrong and Aldrin took off from the Moon's surface to return to earth. The [Nuffield Radio Astronomy Laboratories](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") radio telescope in England recorded transmissions from Luna 15 during its descent, and these were released in July 2009 for the 40th anniversary of Apollo
11.[[46]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

### Prime crew

|                      |
||------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| -                    | -                                                                      |
| Commander            | [Neil Armstrong](# "Contents")<br>Second and last spaceflight          |
| -                    |
| Command Module Pilot | [Michael Collins](# "Contents")<br>Second and last spaceflight         |
| -                    |
| Lunar Module Pilot   | [Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin Jr.](# "Contents")<br>Second and last spaceflight |
| -                    |

The initial crew assignment of Commander [Neil Armstrong](#Background "Contents"), Command Module Pilot (CMP) [Jim Lovell](#Personnel "Contents"), and Lunar Module Pilot (LMP) [Buzz Aldrin](#Personnel "Contents") on the backup crew for
Apollo 9 was officially announced on November 20, 1967.[[47]](#Support_crew "Contents")
Lovell and Aldrin had previously flown together as the crew of [Gemini 12](#Capsule_communicators "Contents"). Due to design and manufacturing delays in the LM,
Apollo 8 and Apollo 9 swapped prime and backup crews, and Armstrong's
crew became the backup for Apollo 8. Based on the normal crew rotation scheme,
Armstrong was then expected to command Apollo 11.[[48]](#Preparations "Contents")

There would be one change. [Michael Collins](#Insignia "Contents"), the CMP on the Apollo 8
crew, began experiencing trouble with his legs. Doctors diagnosed a bony growth between
his fifth and sixth vertebrae, requiring surgery.[[49]](#Mementos "Contents") Lovell
took his place on the Apollo 8 crew, and when Collins recovered he joined Armstrong's
crew as CMP. In the meantime, [Fred Haise](#First-step_decision "Contents") filled in as backup LMP, and Aldrin as backup CMP for Apollo
8.[[50]](#Mission "Contents") Apollo 11 was the second American mission where all
the crew members had prior spaceflight experience,[[51]](#Lunar_descent "Contents")
the first being Apollo 10.[[52]](#Lunar_ascent "Contents") The next was [STS-26](#Columbia_in_lunar_orbit "Contents") in
1988.[[51]](#Splashdown_and_quarantine "Contents")

[Deke Slayton](#Celebrations "Contents") gave Armstrong the option to replace Aldrin with Lovell, since some thought Aldrin was difficult to work with. Armstrong had no issues working with Aldrin but thought it over for a day before declining. He thought Lovell deserved to command his own mission (eventually [Apollo 13](#World_tour
"Contents")).[[53]](#Legacy "Contents")

The Apollo 11 prime crew had none of the close cheerful camaraderie characterized
by that of [Apollo 12](#Cultural_significance "Contents"). Instead, they forged an amiable working relationship. Armstrong in particular was notoriously aloof, but Collins, who considered himself a loner, confessed to rebuffing Aldrin's attempts to create a more personal
relationship.[[54]](#Experiment_results "Contents") Aldrin and Collins described
the crew as "amiable strangers".[[55]](#Anniversary_events "Contents") Armstrong
did not agree with the assessment, and said "all the crews I was on worked very well
together."[[55]](#50th_anniversary "Contents")


### Backup crew

|                      |
||-------------------------------------|-----------|
| -                    | -                                   |
| Commander            | [Jim Lovell](#Notes "Contents")     |
| -                    |
| Command Module Pilot | [William Anders](#Notes "Contents") |
| -                    |
| Lunar Module Pilot   | [Fred Haise](#Citations "Contents") |
| -                    |

The backup crew consisted of Lovell as Commander, [William Anders](#Sources "Contents") as CMP, and Haise as LMP. Anders had flown with Lovell on
Apollo 8.[[51]](#Multimedia "Contents") In early 1969, Anders accepted a job
with the [National Aeronautics and Space Council](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Contents") effective August 1969, and announced he would retire as an astronaut at that time. [Ken Mattingly](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Contents") was moved from the support crew into parallel training with Anders as backup CMP in case Apollo 11 was delayed past its intended July launch date, at which point Anders would be
unavailable.[[56]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "vector-unpinned-container")

Under the normal Apollo crew rotation, Lovell, Mattingly, and Haise would have been
assigned to [Apollo 14](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans"). However, because [Alan Shepard](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans") had only recently returned to flight status and needed additional training, NASA reassigned his crew to Apollo 14 and moved Lovell's crew up to fly [Apollo 13](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans")
instead.[[a]](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Aragonese")
Shortly before launch, Mattingly was replaced by [Jack Swigert](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88_11 "Apollo 11") due to concerns over possible measles
exposure.[[56]](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Asturian")


### Support crew

During Projects Mercury and Gemini, each mission had a prime and a backup crew. For
Apollo, NASA added a third group, the support crew. Their job was to maintain the
flight plan, checklists, and mission rules, and to keep the prime and backup crews
updated on any changes. They also developed procedures—especially for emergencies,
so that by the time the prime and backup crews entered the simulators, they could
focus on practicing and mastering them.[[58]](https://be.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD-11 "Апалон-11 – Belarusian")
The support crew for Apollo 11 was Mattingly, [Ronald Evans](be "Апалон-11"), and [Bill Pogue](https://bg.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 –
Bulgarian").[[59]](br "Apollo 11 – Breton")


### Capsule communicators
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Apollo 11")](https://ca.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Catalan")
CAPCOM [Charles Duke](cs "Apollo 11") (left), with backup crewmembers Lovell and Haise listening in during Apollo 11's descent
The [capsule communicator](cv "Аполлон-11 – Chuvash") (CAPCOM) was an astronaut stationed at the [Mission Control Center](https://cy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Welsh") in [Houston](cy "Apollo 11 – Welsh"), Texas, and was typically the only person permitted to communicate directly with the flight
crew.[[60]](el "Απόλλων 11 – Greek") This practice ensured that messages
came from someone best able to understand the situation in the spacecraft and to
relay guidance from [flight controllers](https://eo.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Esperanto") as clearly as possible. For Apollo 11, the CAPCOMs were backup and support crew members Anders, Evans, Haise, Lovell, and Mattingly, along with [Charles Duke](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apolo_11 "featured article"), [Owen Garriott](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apolo_11 "Apolo 11 – Spanish"), [Don L. Lind](https://et.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Estonian"), [Bruce McCandless II](https://et.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Estonian"), and [Harrison Schmitt](https://eu.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo
11").[[59]](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11")

## Preparations


### Insignia
[![application/atom+xml](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=startup&only=scripts&raw=1&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")
The Apollo 11 insignia. The eagle is carrying an olive branch to represent a peaceful
mission
The Apollo 11 [mission emblem](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") was designed by Collins, who wanted a symbol for "peaceful lunar landing by the United States". At Lovell's suggestion, he chose the [bald eagle](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles"), the [national bird](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") of the United States, as the symbol. Tom Wilson, a simulator instructor, suggested an [olive branch](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") in its beak to represent their peaceful mission. Collins added a lunar background with the Earth in the distance. The sunlight in the image was coming from the wrong direction; the shadow should have been in the lower part of the Earth instead of the
left.[[68]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

Aldrin, Armstrong and Collins decided the Eagle and the Moon would be in their natural
colors, and decided on a blue and gold border. Armstrong was concerned that "eleven"
would not be understood by non-English speakers, so they went with "Apollo 11",[[68]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
and they decided not to put their names on the patch, so it would "be representative
of *everyone* who had worked toward a lunar landing".[[69]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

An illustrator at the [Manned Spacecraft Center](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") (MSC) did the artwork, which was then sent off to NASA officials for
approval.[[68]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
The design was rejected. [Bob Gilruth](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), the director of the MSC felt the talons of the eagle looked "too
warlike".[[70]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
After some discussion, the olive branch was moved to the talons.[[70]](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
When the [Eisenhower dollar coin](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") was released in 1971, the patch design provided the eagle for its reverse
side.[[71]](//upload.wikimedia.org "Wikipedia (en)") The design was also used for
the smaller [Susan B. Anthony dollar](/w/rest.php/v1/search "Wikipedia (en)") unveiled in 1979.[[72]](/w/index.php?title=Special:RecentChanges&feed=atom ">
<link rel=")


### Call signs
[![](/static/images/icons/enwiki-25.svg "Main menu")](#bodyContent "Main menu")
The original cockpit of the command module (CM) with three seats, photographed from
above. It is located in the [National Air and Space Museum](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"). The very high resolution image was produced in 2007 by the [Smithsonian Institution](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]").
After the crew of Apollo 10 named their spacecraft *Charlie Brown* and *Snoopy*,
assistant manager for public affairs [Julian Scheer](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") wrote to [George Low](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), the Manager of the Apollo Spacecraft Program Office at the MSC, to suggest the Apollo 11 crew be less flippant in naming their craft. The name
*Snowcone* was used for the CM and *Haystack* was used for the LM in both internal
and external communications during early mission planning.[[73]](/wiki/Special:Random "Visit a randomly selected article [x]")

The LM was named *[Eagle](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contact_us "Learn about Wikipedia and how it works")*
after the motif which was featured prominently on the mission insignia. At Scheer's
suggestion, the CM was named *[Columbia](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia")*
after *[Columbiad](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia")*,
the giant cannon that launched a spacecraft (also from Florida) in [Jules Verne](/wiki/Help:Introduction "Learn how to edit Wikipedia")'s 1865 novel *[From the Earth to the Moon](/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_portal "The hub for
editors")*. It also referred to [Columbia](/wiki/Special:RecentChanges "A list of recent changes to Wikipedia [r]"), a historical name of the United
States.[[74]](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")[[75]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
In Collins' 1976 book, he said *Columbia* was in reference to [Christopher Columbus](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia
[f]").[[76]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")


### Mementos
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail " title=")](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
Apollo 11 space-flown silver [Robbins medallion](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
The astronauts had [personal preference kits](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") (PPKs), small bags containing personal items of significance they wanted to take with them on the
mission.[[77]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "You're encouraged to log in; however, it's not mandatory. [o]")
Five 0.5-pound (0.23 kg) PPKs were carried on Apollo 11: three (one for each
astronaut) were stowed on *Columbia* before launch, and two on *Eagle*.[[78]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")

Neil Armstrong's LM PPK contained a piece of wood from the [Wright brothers](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=")' 1903 *[Wright Flyer](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 "
title=")*'s left propeller and a piece of fabric from its wing,[[79]](# "Contents")
along with a diamond-studded [astronaut pin](# "Contents") originally given to Slayton by the widows of the
Apollo 1 crew. This pin had been intended to be flown on that mission and given
to Slayton afterwards, but following the disastrous launch pad fire and subsequent
funerals, the widows gave the pin to Slayton. Armstrong took it with him on Apollo
11.[[80]](#Background "Contents")


### Site selection


[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Preparations "Contents")


[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Mementos "Contents")


[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Pre-launch "Contents")


[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Lunar_descent "Contents")


[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Lunar_ascent "Contents")


[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Return "Contents")

A map of the Moon showing prospective landing sites for Apollo 11. Site 2 in the
[Sea of Tranquility](#World_tour "Contents") was chosen.  
NASA's Apollo Site Selection Board announced five potential landing sites on February
8, 1968. These were the result of two years' worth of studies based on high-resolution
photography of the lunar surface by the five uncrewed probes of the [Lunar Orbiter program](#World_tour "Contents") and information about surface conditions provided by the [Surveyor program](#Legacy
"Contents").[[81]](#Cultural_significance "Contents") The best Earth-bound telescopes
could not resolve features with the resolution Project Apollo required.[[82]](#Experiment_results "Contents")
The landing site had to be close to the lunar equator to minimize the amount of propellant
required, clear of obstacles to minimize maneuvering, and flat to simplify the task
of the landing radar. Scientific value was not a consideration.[[83]](#Anniversary_events "Contents")

Areas that appeared promising on photographs taken on Earth were often found to be
totally unacceptable. The original requirement that the site be free of craters had
to be relaxed, as no such site was found.[[84]](#Films_and_documentaries "Contents")
Five sites were considered: Sites 1 and 2 were in the Sea of Tranquility
(*[Mare Tranquillitatis](#See_also "Contents")*); Site 3 was in the Central
Bay (*[Sinus Medii](#Notes "Contents")*); and Sites 4 and 5 were in the
Ocean of Storms (*[Oceanus Procellarum](#Notes "Contents")*).[[81]](#Citations "Contents")The
final site selection was based on seven criteria:

- The site needed to be smooth, with relatively few craters;
- with approach paths free of large hills, tall cliffs or deep craters that might confuse the landing radar and cause it to issue incorrect readings;
- reachable with a minimum amount of propellant;
- allowing for delays in the launch countdown;
- providing the Apollo spacecraft with a free-return trajectory, one that would allow it to coast around the Moon and safely return to Earth without requiring any engine firings should a problem arise on the way to the Moon;
- with good visibility during the landing approach, meaning the Sun would be between 7 and 20 degrees behind the LM; and
- a general slope of less than two degrees in the landing area.[[81]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Contents")

The requirement for the Sun angle was particularly restrictive, limiting the launch
date to one day per month.[[81]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "button")
A landing just after dawn was chosen to limit the temperature extremes the astronauts
would experience.[[85]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans")
The Apollo Site Selection Board selected Site 2, with Sites 3 and 5
as backups in the event of the launch being delayed. In May 1969, Apollo 10's lunar
module flew to within 15 kilometers (9.3 mi) of Site 2, and reported it
was acceptable.[[86]](https://ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88_11 "أبولو 11 –
Arabic")[[87]](https://as.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%AA%27%E0%A6%B2%27_%E0%A7%A7%E0%A7%A7 "এপ'ল' ১১ – Assamese")


### First-step decision

During the first press conference after the Apollo 11 crew was announced, the first
question was, "Which one of you gentlemen will be the first man to step onto the
lunar surface?"[[88]](https://ban.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Balinese")[[89]](https://be.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD-11 "Апалон-11 – Belarusian")
Slayton told the reporter it had not been decided, and Armstrong added that it was
"not based on individual desire".[[88]](bn "অ্যাপোলো ১১")

One of the first versions of the egress checklist had the lunar module pilot exit
the spacecraft before the commander, which matched what had been done on Gemini missions,[[90]](https://ceb.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_XI "Apollo XI – Cebuano")
where the commander had never performed the spacewalk.[[91]](https://cv.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD-11 "Аполлон-11 – Chuvash")
Reporters wrote in early 1969 that Aldrin would be the first man to walk on the Moon,
and Associate Administrator [George Mueller](https://cy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Welsh") told reporters he would be first as well. Aldrin heard that Armstrong would be the first because Armstrong was a civilian, which made Aldrin livid. Aldrin attempted to persuade other Lunar Module pilots he should be first, but they responded cynically about what they perceived as a lobbying campaign. Attempting to stem interdepartmental conflict, Slayton told Aldrin that Armstrong would be first since he was the commander. The decision was announced in a press conference on April 14,
1969.[[92]](https://eo.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Esperanto")

For decades, Aldrin believed the final decision was largely driven by the Lunar Module's
hatch location. Because the astronauts had their spacesuits on and the spacecraft
was so small, maneuvering to exit the spacecraft was difficult. The crew tried a
simulation in which Aldrin left the spacecraft first, but he damaged the simulator
while attempting to egress. While this was enough for mission planners to make their
decision, Aldrin and Armstrong were left in the dark on the decision until late spring.[[93]](fa "آپولو ۱۱ – Persian")
Slayton told Armstrong the plan was to have him leave the spacecraft first, if he
agreed. Armstrong said, "Yes, that's the way to do it."[[94]](fy "Apollo 11")

The media accused Armstrong of exercising his commander's prerogative to exit the
spacecraft first.[[95]](https://gv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "એપોલો ૧૧")
[Chris Kraft](https://gv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Manx") revealed in his 2001 autobiography that a meeting occurred between Gilruth, Slayton, Low, and himself to make sure Aldrin would not be the first to walk on the Moon. They argued that the first person to walk on the Moon should be like [Charles Lindbergh](ha "Apollo 11 – Hausa"), a calm and quiet person. They made the decision to change the flight plan so the commander was the first to egress from the
spacecraft.[[96]](https://hr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Croatian")


### Pre-launch
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Ապոլոն 11 – Armenian")](hu "Apollo–11 – Hungarian")
Saturn V SA-506, the rocket carrying the Apollo 11 spacecraft, moves out of the [Vehicle Assembly Building](https://io.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Ido") towards [Launch Complex 39](https://is.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tungllendingin_(1969) "Tungllendingin (1969) – Icelandic").
The ascent stage of [LM-5 *Eagle*](is "Tungllendingin (1969)") arrived at the [Kennedy Space Center](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article") on January 8, 1969, followed by the descent stage four days later, and [CSM-107
*Columbia*](it "Apollo 11 – Italian") on January 23.[[6]](https://jv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Javanese")
There were several differences between *Eagle* and Apollo 10's LM-4 *Snoopy*; *Eagle*
had a VHF radio antenna to facilitate communication with the astronauts during their
EVA on the lunar surface; a lighter ascent engine; more thermal protection on the
landing gear; and a package of scientific experiments known as the [Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package](ka "აპოლო 11") (EASEP). The only change in the configuration of the command module was the removal of some insulation from the forward
hatch.[[97]](ko "아폴로 11호")[[98]](https://ku.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Kurdish")
The CSM was mated on January 29, and moved from the [Operations and Checkout Building](ku "Apollo 11") to the [Vehicle Assembly Building](https://la.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latin") on April
14.[[6]](lmo "Apollo XI")

The [S-IVB](https://lt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Lithuanian") third stage of Saturn V AS-506 had arrived on January 18, followed by the [S-II](https://lv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latvian") second stage on February 6, [S-IC](https://lv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latvian") first stage on February 20, and the [Saturn V Instrument Unit](lv "Apollo 11") on February 27. At 12:30 on May 20, the
5,443-tonne (5,357-long-ton; 6,000-short-ton) assembly departed the Vehicle Assembly
Building atop the [crawler-transporter](https://mk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 – Macedonian"), bound for Launch Pad 39A, part of [Launch Complex 39](https://mk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 – Macedonian"), while Apollo 10 was still on its way to the Moon. A countdown test commenced on June 26, and concluded on July 2. The launch complex was floodlit on the night of July 15, when the crawler-transporter carried the [mobile service structure](https://ml.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%B4%85%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8D%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8B%E0%B4%B3%E0%B5%8B_11 "അപ്പോളോ 11 – Malayalam") back to its parking
area.[[6]](https://mr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8B_%E0%A5%A7%E0%A5%A7 "अपोलो ११ – Marathi")
In the early hours of the morning, the fuel tanks of the S-II and S-IVB stages were
filled with [liquid hydrogen](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available
skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard").[[99]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
Fueling was completed by three hours before launch.[[100]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Launch operations were partly automated, with 43 programs written in the [ATOLL programming language](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 -
Wikipedia").[[101]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

Slayton roused the crew shortly after 04:00, and they showered, shaved, and had the
traditional pre-flight breakfast of steak and eggs with Slayton and the backup crew.
They then donned their space suits and began breathing pure oxygen. At 06:30, they
headed out to Launch Complex 39.[[102]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Haise entered *Columbia* about three hours and ten minutes before launch time. Along
with a technician, he helped Armstrong into the left-hand couch at 06:54. Five minutes
later, Collins joined him, taking up his position on the right-hand couch. Finally,
Aldrin entered, taking the center couch.[[100]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Haise left around two hours and ten minutes before launch.[[103]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
The closeout crew sealed the hatch, and the cabin was purged and pressurized. The
closeout crew then left the launch complex about an hour before launch time. The
countdown became automated at three minutes and twenty seconds before launch time.[[100]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Over 450 personnel were at the consoles in the [firing room](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 -
Wikipedia").[[99]](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")


## Mission


### Launch and flight to lunar orbit
[![application/atom+xml](/static/images/icons/enwiki-25.svg "Wikipedia Atom feed")](//en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=rsd "Wikipedia Atom feed")
The Apollo 11 Saturn V space vehicle lifts off with astronauts Neil A. Armstrong,
Michael Collins and Edwin E. Aldrin Jr. at 9:32 am. EDT July 16, 1969, from
Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39A.
An estimated one million spectators watched the launch of Apollo 11 from the highways
and beaches in the vicinity of the launch site. Dignitaries included the [Chief of Staff of the United States Army](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), [General](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") [William Westmoreland](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), four [cabinet members](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), 19 [state governors](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), 40 [mayors](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), 60 ambassadors and 200 [congressmen](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"). Vice President [Spiro Agnew](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") viewed the launch with former president [Lyndon B. Johnson](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") and his wife [Lady Bird Johnson](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page
[z]").[[99]](/wiki/Wikipedia:About "Learn about Wikipedia and how it works")[[104]](/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_portal "The hub for editors")
Around 3,500 media representatives were present.[[105]](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")
About two-thirds were from the United States; the rest came from 55 other countries.
The launch was televised live in 33 countries, with an estimated 25 million
viewers in the United States alone. Millions more around the world listened to radio
broadcasts.[[104]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia
[f]")[[99]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
President [Richard Nixon](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") viewed the launch from his office in the [White House](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") with his NASA liaison officer, Apollo astronaut [Frank Borman](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "
title=").[[106]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
Lodging near Cape Canaveral was reported as being booked months ahead in advance
for the launch by a Florida newspaper.[[107]](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=")

Saturn V AS-506 launched Apollo 11 on July 16, 1969, at 13:32:00 [UTC](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 "You are encouraged to create an account and log in; however, it is not mandatory") (9:32:00 [EDT](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 "
title=")).[[6]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options")
At 13.2 seconds into the flight, the vehicle began to [roll](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") into its [flight azimuth](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") of 72.058°. Full shutdown of the first-stage engines occurred about
2 minutes and 42 seconds into the mission, followed by separation of the S-IC
and ignition of the S-II engines. The second stage engines then cut off and separated
at about 9 minutes and 8 seconds, allowing the first ignition of the S-IVB
engine a few seconds later.[[8]](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=")

Apollo 11 entered a [near-circular Earth orbit](# "You're encouraged to log in; however, it's not mandatory. [o]") at an altitude of
100.4 nautical miles (185.9 km) by 98.9 nautical miles (183.2 km), twelve
minutes into its flight. After one and a half orbits, which took around two and a
half hours, a second ignition of the S-IVB engine pushed the spacecraft onto its
trajectory toward the Moon with the [trans-lunar injection](# "Contents") (TLI) burn, which took about 5 minutes and 47 seconds and started at 16:16:16 UTC. About 30 minutes later, with Collins in the left seat and at the controls, the [transposition, docking, and extraction](# "Contents") maneuver was performed. This involved separating
*Columbia* from the spent S-IVB stage, turning around, and docking with *Eagle*
still attached to the stage. After the LM was extracted, the combined spacecraft
headed for the Moon, while the rocket stage flew on a trajectory past the Moon.[[108]](#Prime_crew
"Contents")[[8]](#Capsule_communicators "Contents") This was done to avoid the third
stage colliding with the spacecraft, the Earth, or the Moon. A [slingshot effect](#Flight_directors "Contents") from passing around the Moon threw it into an [orbit around the Sun](#Flight_directors
"Contents").[[109]](#Insignia "Contents")

On July 19 at 17:21:50 UTC, Apollo 11 passed behind the Moon and fired its service
propulsion engine to enter [lunar orbit](#Insignia "Contents").[[8]](#Site_selection
"Contents")[[110]](#First-step_decision "Contents") In the thirty orbits that followed,
the crew saw passing views of their landing site in the southern Sea of Tranquility
about 12 miles (19 km) southwest of the crater [Sabine D](#Mission "Contents"). The site was selected in part because it had been characterized as relatively flat and smooth by the automated [Ranger 8](#Launch_and_flight_to_lunar_orbit "Contents") and [Surveyor 5](#Launch_and_flight_to_lunar_orbit "Contents") landers and the Lunar Orbiter mapping spacecraft, and because it was unlikely to present major landing or EVA
challenges.[[111]](#Lunar_descent "Contents") It lay about 25 kilometers (16 mi)
southeast of the Surveyor 5 landing site, and 68 kilometers (42 mi) southwest
of Ranger 8's crash site.[[112]](#Splashdown_and_quarantine "Contents")


### Lunar descent
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Celebrations "Contents")
[*Columbia*](#Cultural_significance "Contents") in lunar orbit, photographed from [*Eagle*](#Cultural_significance "Contents")
At 12:52:00 UTC on July 20, Aldrin and Armstrong entered [*Eagle*](#Spacecraft "Contents"), and began the final preparations for lunar
descent.[[8]](#Experiment_results "Contents") At 17:44:00 *Eagle* separated from
*Columbia*.[[13]](#Anniversary_events "Contents") Collins, alone aboard *Columbia*,
inspected *Eagle* as it pirouetted before him to ensure the craft was not damaged,
and that the landing gear was correctly deployed.[[113]](#Films_and_documentaries "Contents")[[114]](#Notes "Contents")
Armstrong exclaimed: "The *Eagle* has wings!"[[114]](#External_links "Contents")

As the descent began, Armstrong and Aldrin found themselves passing landmarks on
the surface two or three seconds early, and reported that they were "long"; they
would land miles west of their target point. *Eagle* was traveling too fast. The
problem could have been [mascons](#Multimedia "Contents")—concen­tra­tions of
high mass in a region or regions of the Moon's crust that contains a [gravitational anomaly](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Contents"), potentially altering
*Eagle*'s trajectory. Flight Director Gene Kranz speculated that it could have resulted
from extra air pressure in the docking tunnel, or a result of *Eagle*'s pirouette
maneuver.[[115]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans")[[116]](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Aragonese")

Five minutes into the descent burn, and 6,000 feet (1,800 m) above the surface
of the Moon, the [LM guidance computer](as "এপ'ল' ১১ – Assamese") (LGC) distracted the crew with the first of several unexpected 1201 and 1202 program alarms. Inside Mission Control Center, computer engineer [Jack Garman](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Asturian") told [Guidance Officer](ast "Apollo 11 – Asturian") [Steve Bales](https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollon_11 "Apollon 11 – Azerbaijani") it was safe to continue the descent, and this was relayed to the crew. The program alarms indicated "executive overflows", meaning the guidance computer could not complete all its tasks in real-time and had to postpone some of
them.[[117]](https://be-tarask.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D1%91%D0%BD-11 "Апалён-11 – Belarusian (Taraškievica
orthography)")[[118]](bg "Аполо 11") [Margaret Hamilton](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%85%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8B_%E0%A7%A7%E0%A7%A7 "অ্যাপোলো ১১ – Bangla"), the Director of Apollo Flight Computer Programming at the [MIT](bn "অ্যাপোলো ১১") [Charles Stark Draper Laboratory](https://br.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Breton") later recalled:
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Apollo 11 – Bosnian")](https://bs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Bosnian")
[*Eagle*](https://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article") in [lunar orbit](https://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article") photographed from
[*Columbia*](cs "Apollo 11")
> To blame the computer for the Apollo 11 problems is like blaming the person who
spots a fire and calls the fire department. Actually, the computer was programmed
to do more than recognize error conditions. A complete set of recovery programs was
incorporated into the software. The software's action, in this case, was to eliminate
lower priority tasks and re-establish the more important ones. The computer, rather
than almost forcing an abort, prevented an abort. If the computer hadn't recognized
this problem and taken recovery action, I doubt if Apollo 11 would have been the
successful Moon landing it was.[[119]](https://et.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Estonian")

During the mission, the cause was diagnosed as the rendezvous radar switch being
in the wrong position, causing the computer to process data from both the rendezvous
and landing radars at the same time.[[120]](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo
11")[[121]](https://fy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article") Software engineer
[Don Eyles](https://ga.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11") concluded in a 2005 Guidance and Control Conference paper that the problem was due to a hardware design bug previously seen during testing of the first uncrewed LM in [Apollo 5](ga "Apollo 11"). Having the rendezvous radar on (so it was warmed up in case of an emergency landing abort) should have been irrelevant to the computer, but an electrical phasing mismatch between two parts of the rendezvous radar system could cause the stationary antenna to appear to the computer as dithering back and forth between two positions, depending upon how the hardware randomly powered up. The extra spurious [cycle stealing](https://gu.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%AA%8F%E0%AA%AA%E0%AB%8B%E0%AA%B2%E0%AB%8B_%E0%AB%A7%E0%AB%A7 "એપોલો ૧૧ – Gujarati"), as the rendezvous radar updated an involuntary counter, caused the computer
alarms.[[122]](https://gv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Manx")


### Landing
Armstrong pilots *Eagle* to its landing on the Moon, July 20, 1969.
When Armstrong again looked outside, he saw that the computer's landing system was
targeting a boulder-strewn area just north and east of a 300-foot-diameter (91 m)
crater (later determined to be [West crater](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%95%84%ED%8F%B4%EB%A1%9C_11%ED%98%B8 "아폴로 11호 – Korean")), so he took semi-automatic
control.[[123]](https://la.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latin")[[124]](https://lv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latvian")
Armstrong considered landing short of the boulder field so they could collect geological
samples from it, but could not since their horizontal velocity was too high. Throughout
the descent, Aldrin called out navigation data to Armstrong, who was busy piloting
*Eagle*.[[125]](mk "Аполо 11 – Macedonian")

Armstrong found a clear patch of ground and maneuvered the spacecraft towards it.
As he got closer, now 250 feet (76 m) above the surface, he discovered his new
landing site had a crater in it.  Now 107 feet (33 m) above the surface, Armstrong
knew their propellant supply was dwindling and was determined to land at the first
possible landing site. He cleared the crater and found another patch of level ground.
They were now 100 feet (30 m) from the surface, with only 90 seconds of propellant
remaining. Lunar dust kicked up by the LM's engine began to impair his ability to
determine the spacecraft's motion. Some large rocks jutted out of the dust cloud,
and Armstrong focused on them during his descent so he could determine the spacecraft's
speed.[[126]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

A light informed Aldrin that at least one of the 67-inch (170 cm) probes hanging
from *Eagle*'s footpads had touched the surface a few moments before the landing
and he said: "Contact light!" Armstrong was supposed to immediately shut the engine
down, as the engineers suspected the pressure caused by the engine's own exhaust
reflecting off the lunar surface could make it explode, but he forgot. Three seconds
later, *Eagle* landed and Armstrong shut the engine down.[[127]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Aldrin immediately said "Okay, engine stop. ACA—out of [detent](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")." Armstrong acknowledged: "Out of detent. Auto." Aldrin continued: "Mode control—both auto. Descent engine command override off. Engine arm—off. 413 is
in."[[128]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
[![application/atom+xml](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=startup&only=scripts&raw=1&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
