The landing site relative to [West crater](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
ACA was the [Attitude Control Assembly](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")—the LM's control stick. Output went to the LGC to command the [reaction control system](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") (RCS) jets to fire. "Out of Detent" meant the stick had moved away from its centered position; it was spring-centered like the turn indicator in a car. Address 413 of the [Abort Guidance System](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") (AGS) contained the variable that indicated the LM had
landed.[[10]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

*Eagle* landed at 20:17:40 UTC on Sunday July 20 with 216 pounds (98 kg) of
usable fuel remaining. Information available to the crew and mission controllers
during the landing showed the LM had enough fuel for another 25 seconds of powered
flight before an abort without touchdown would have become unsafe,[[10]](//en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=rsd "Wikipedia Atom
feed")[[129]](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu") but post-mission analysis showed that
the real figure was probably closer to 50 seconds.[[130]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")
Apollo 11 landed with less fuel than most subsequent missions, and the astronauts
encountered a premature low fuel warning. This was later found to be the result of
the propellant [sloshing](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") more than expected, uncovering a fuel sensor. On subsequent missions, extra [anti-slosh baffles](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") were added to the tanks to prevent
this.[[10]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")

Armstrong acknowledged Aldrin's completion of the post-landing checklist with "Engine
arm is off", before responding to the CAPCOM, Charles Duke, with the words, "Houston,
[Tranquility Base](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") here. The *[Eagle](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")*
has landed." Armstrong's unrehearsed change of call sign from "Eagle" to "Tranquility
Base" emphasized to listeners that landing was complete and successful.[[131]](/wiki/Special:Random "Visit a randomly selected article
[x]")[*[better source needed](/wiki/Special:RecentChanges "The hub for editors")*]
Duke expressed the relief at Mission Control: "Roger, Twan—Tranquility, we copy
you on the ground. You got a bunch of guys about to turn blue. We're breathing again.
Thanks a lot."[[10]](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")[[132]](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")
A [3-D](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") view from the [Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") (LRO) of the Apollo 11 landing site
Two and a half hours after landing, before preparations began for the EVA, Aldrin
radioed to Earth:

> This is the LM pilot. I'd like to take this opportunity to ask every person listening
in, whoever and wherever they may be, to pause for a moment and contemplate the events
of the past few hours and to give thanks in his or her own way.[[133]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options")

He then took [communion](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") privately. At this time NASA was still fighting a lawsuit brought by atheist [Madalyn Murray O'Hair](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") (who had objected to the
[Apollo 8 crew reading from the Book of Genesis](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")) demanding that their astronauts refrain from broadcasting religious activities while in space. For this reason, Aldrin chose to refrain from directly mentioning taking communion on the Moon. Aldrin was an elder at the [Webster](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") [Presbyterian Church](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), and his communion kit was prepared by the pastor of the church, Dean Woodruff. Webster Presbyterian possesses the chalice used on the Moon and commemorates the event each year on the Sunday closest to July
20.[[134]](# "Contents") The schedule for the mission called for the astronauts
to follow the landing with a five-hour sleep period, but they chose to begin preparations
for the EVA early, thinking they would be unable to sleep.[[135]](# "Contents")


### Lunar surface operations

Main article: [Tranquility Base](#Prime_crew "Contents")
Preparations for [Neil Armstrong](#Prime_crew "Contents") and [Buzz Aldrin](#Prime_crew "Contents") to walk on the Moon began at 23:43
UTC.[[13]](#Capsule_communicators "Contents") These took longer than expected; three
and a half hours instead of two.[[136]](#Flight_directors "Contents") During training
on Earth, everything required had been neatly laid out in advance, but on the Moon
the cabin contained a large number of other items as well, such as checklists, food
packets, and tools.[[137]](#Insignia "Contents") Six hours and thirty-nine minutes
after landing, Armstrong and Aldrin were ready to go outside, and *Eagle* was depressurized.[[138]](#Site_selection "Contents")

*Eagle*'s hatch was opened at 02:39:33.[[13]](#Launch_and_flight_to_lunar_orbit "Contents")
Armstrong initially had some difficulties squeezing through the hatch with his [portable life support system](#Launch_and_flight_to_lunar_orbit "Contents")
(PLSS).[[136]](#Lunar_descent "Contents") Some of the highest heart rates recorded
from Apollo astronauts occurred during LM egress and ingress.[[139]](#Columbia_in_lunar_orbit "Contents")
At 02:51 Armstrong began his descent to the lunar surface. The remote-control unit
on his chest kept him from seeing his feet. Climbing down the nine-rung ladder, Armstrong
pulled a D-ring to deploy the modular equipment stowage assembly (MESA) folded against
*Eagle*'s side and activate the TV camera.[[140]](#Celebrations "Contents")[[141]](#World_tour "Contents")

Apollo 11 used [slow-scan television](#World_tour "Contents") (TV) incompatible with broadcast TV, so it was displayed on a special monitor and a conventional TV camera viewed this monitor (thus, a broadcast of a broadcast), significantly reducing the quality of the
picture.[[142]](#Cultural_significance "Contents") The signal was received at [Goldstone](#Cultural_significance "Contents") in the United States, but with better fidelity by [Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station](#Spacecraft "Contents") near [Canberra](#Spacecraft "Contents") in Australia. Minutes later the feed was switched to the more sensitive [Parkes radio telescope](#Moon_rocks "Contents") in
Australia.[[143]](#Lunar_Module_Eagle_memorabilia "Contents") Despite some technical
and weather difficulties, black and white images of the first lunar EVA were received
and broadcast to at least 600 million people on Earth.[[143]](#50th_anniversary "Contents")
Copies of this video in broadcast format were saved and are widely available, but
[recordings of the original slow scan source transmission from the lunar surface](#Films_and_documentaries "Contents") were likely destroyed during routine magnetic tape re-use at
NASA.[[142]](#See_also "Contents")
Video of Neil Armstrong and the first step on the Moon

![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Апалён-11 – Belarusian (Taraškievica orthography)")

[That's one small step ...](https://bg.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 – Bulgarian")


---
*Problems playing this file? See [media help](hu "Apollo–11").*
After describing the surface dust as "very fine-grained" and "almost like a powder",[[141]](https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Indonesian")
at 02:56:15,[[144]](https://is.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tungllendingin_(1969) "Tungllendingin (1969) – Icelandic")
six and a half hours after landing, Armstrong stepped off *Eagle*'s landing pad and
declared: "That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind."[[b]](kk "Аполлон 11 –
Kazakh")[[146]](https://ks.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A7%D9%BE%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88_%DB%B1%DB%B1 "اپولو ۱۱ –
Kashmiri")[[147]](https://ku.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Kurdish")

Armstrong intended to say "That's one small step for a man", but the word "a" is
not audible in the transmission, and thus was not initially reported by most observers
of the live broadcast. When later asked about his quote, Armstrong said he believed
he said "for a man", and subsequent printed versions of the quote included the "a"
in square brackets. One explanation for the absence may be that his accent caused
him to slur the words "for a" together; another is the intermittent nature of the
audio and video links to Earth, partly because of storms near Parkes Observatory.
A more recent digital analysis of the tape claims to reveal the "a" may have been
spoken but obscured by static. Other analysis points to the claims of static and
slurring as "face-saving fabrication", and that Armstrong himself later admitted
to misspeaking the line.[[148]](https://lv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 –
Latvian")[[149]](mg "Apollo 11")[[150]](https://mk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 – Macedonian")

About seven minutes after stepping onto the Moon's surface, Armstrong collected a
contingency soil sample using a sample bag on a stick. He then folded the bag and
tucked it into a pocket on his right thigh. This was to guarantee there would be
some lunar soil brought back in case an emergency required the astronauts to abandon
the EVA and return to the LM.[[151]](https://mr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8B_%E0%A5%A7%E0%A5%A7 "अपोलो ११ – Marathi")
Twelve minutes after the sample was collected,[[146]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
he removed the TV camera from the MESA and made a panoramic sweep, then mounted it
on a tripod.[[136]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
The TV camera cable remained partly coiled and presented a tripping hazard throughout
the EVA. Still photography was accomplished with a [Hasselblad](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") camera that could be operated hand-held or mounted on Armstrong's [Apollo space suit](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ext.globalCssJs.user.styles").[[152]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Aldrin joined Armstrong on the surface. He described the view with the simple phrase:
"Magnificent desolation."[[141]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

Armstrong said moving in the [lunar gravity](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), one-sixth of Earth's, was "even perhaps easier than the
simulations ... It's absolutely no trouble to walk around."[[141]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Aldrin joined him on the surface and tested methods for moving around, including
two-footed kangaroo hops. The PLSS backpack created a tendency to tip backward, but
neither astronaut had serious problems maintaining balance. Loping became the preferred
method of movement. The astronauts reported that they needed to plan their movements
six or seven steps ahead. The fine soil was quite slippery. Aldrin remarked that
moving from sunlight into *Eagle*'s shadow produced no temperature change inside
the suit, but the helmet was warmer in sunlight, so he felt cooler in shadow.[[141]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
The MESA failed to provide a stable work platform and was in shadow, slowing work
somewhat. As they worked, the moonwalkers kicked up gray dust, which soiled the outer
part of their suits.[[152]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
[![application/atom+xml](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=startup&only=scripts&raw=1&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Aldrin salutes the deployed United States flag on the [lunar surface](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia").
The astronauts planted the [Lunar Flag Assembly](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") containing a [flag of the United States](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") on the lunar surface, in clear view of the TV camera. Aldrin remembered, "Of all the jobs I had to do on the Moon the one I wanted to go the smoothest was the flag
raising."[[153]](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") But the astronauts
struggled with the telescoping rod and could only insert the pole about 2 inches
(5 cm) into the hard lunar surface. Aldrin was afraid it might topple in front
of TV viewers, but gave "a crisp West Point salute".[[153]](/w/index.php?title=Special:RecentChanges&feed=atom ">
<link rel=")

Before Aldrin could take a photo of Armstrong with the flag, President Richard Nixon
spoke to them through a telephone-radio transmission, which Nixon called "the most
historic phone call ever made from the White House."[[154]](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu")
Nixon originally had a long speech prepared to read during the phone call, but Frank
Borman, who was at the White House as a NASA liaison during Apollo 11, convinced
Nixon to keep his words brief.[[155]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")

> **Nixon:** Hello, Neil and Buzz. I'm talking to you by telephone from the Oval
Room at the White House. And this certainly has to be the most historic telephone
call ever made from the White House. I just can't tell you how proud we all are of
what you have done. For every American, this has to be the proudest day of our lives.
And for people all over the world, I am sure that they too join with Americans in
recognizing what an immense feat this is. Because of what you have done, the heavens
have become a part of man's world. And as you talk to us from the Sea of Tranquility,
it inspires us to redouble our efforts to bring peace and tranquility to Earth. For
one priceless moment in the whole history of man, all the people on this Earth are
truly one: one in their pride in what you have done, and one in our prayers that
you will return safely to Earth.
>
> **Armstrong:** Thank you, Mr. President. It's a great honor and privilege for us
to be here, representing not only the United States, but men of peace of all nations,
and with interest and a curiosity, and men with a vision for the future. It's an
honor for us to be able to participate here today.
>
> **Nixon:** Thank you very much, and I look forward, all of us look forward, to
seeing you on the Hornet on Thursday.[[156]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and
color")[[157]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail " title=")](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
Aldrin's bootprint, part of an experiment to test the properties of the lunar [regolith](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
They deployed the [EASEP](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title="), which included a [Passive Seismic Experiment Package](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") used to measure [moonquakes](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") and a [retroreflector](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") array used for the [lunar laser ranging experiment](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 "
title=").[[158]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")
Then Armstrong walked 196 feet (60 m) from the LM to take photographs at the
rim of [Little West Crater](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
while Aldrin collected two [core samples](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="). He used the [geologist's hammer](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") to pound in the tubes—the only time the hammer was used on Apollo 11—but was unable to penetrate more than
6 inches (15 cm) deep. The astronauts then collected rock samples using scoops
and tongs on extension handles.[[159]](# "Contents")

Many of the surface activities took longer than expected, so they had to stop documenting
sample collection halfway through the allotted 34 minutes. Aldrin shoveled 6 kilograms
(13 lb) of soil into the box of rocks to pack them in tightly.[[159]](#Prime_crew "Contents")
Two types of rocks were found in the geological samples: [basalt](#Prime_crew "Contents") and [breccia](#Prime_crew
"Contents").[[160]](#Backup_crew "Contents") Three new minerals were discovered
in the rock samples collected by the astronauts: [armalcolite](#Support_crew "Contents"), [tranquillityite](#Support_crew "Contents"), and [pyroxferroite](#Capsule_communicators "Contents"). Armalcolite was named after Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins. All have subsequently been found on
Earth.[[161]](#Flight_directors "Contents")
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Other_key_personnel "Contents")
[The plaque](#Insignia "Contents") left on the ladder of *Eagle*
While on the surface, Armstrong uncovered a [plaque](#Insignia "Contents") mounted on the LM ladder, bearing two drawings of Earth (of the Western and Eastern Hemispheres), an inscription, and signatures of the astronauts and President Nixon. The inscription read:

> Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon July 1969, A. D. We
came in peace for all mankind.[[141]](#Pre-launch "Contents")

At the behest of the [Nixon administration](#Pre-launch "Contents") to add a reference to God, NASA included the vague date as a reason to include A.D., which stands for [Anno Domini](#Mission "Contents") ("in the year of our
Lord").[[162]](#Lunar_descent "Contents")

Mission Control used a coded phrase to warn Armstrong his metabolic rates were high,
and that he should slow down. He was moving rapidly from task to task as time ran
out. As metabolic rates remained generally lower than expected for both astronauts
throughout the walk, Mission Control granted the astronauts a 15-minute extension.[[158]](#Lunar_surface_operations "Contents")
In a 2010 interview, Armstrong explained that NASA limited the first moonwalk's time
and distance because there was no empirical proof of how much cooling water the astronauts'
PLSS backpacks would consume to handle their body heat generation while working on
the Moon.[[163]](#Columbia_in_lunar_orbit "Contents")


### Lunar ascent

Aldrin entered *Eagle* first. With some difficulty the astronauts lifted film and
two sample boxes containing 21.55 kilograms (47.5 lb) of lunar surface material
to the LM hatch using a flat cable pulley device called the Lunar Equipment Conveyor
(LEC). This proved to be an inefficient tool, and later missions preferred to carry
equipment and samples up to the LM by hand.[[136]](#World_tour "Contents") Armstrong
reminded Aldrin of a bag of memorial items in his sleeve pocket, and Aldrin tossed
the bag down. Armstrong then jumped onto the ladder's third rung, and climbed into
the LM. After transferring to LM [life support](#Legacy "Contents"), the explorers lightened the ascent stage for the return to lunar orbit by tossing out their PLSS backpacks, lunar overshoes, an empty Hasselblad camera, and other
equipment.[[164]](#Cultural_significance "Contents")[[165]](#Spacecraft "Contents")
The hatch was closed again at 05:11:13. They then pressurized the LM and settled
down to sleep.[[166]](#Experiment_results "Contents")
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Moonwalk_camera "Contents")
Aldrin next to the Passive Seismic Experiment Package with the [Lunar Module](#40th_anniversary "Contents")
*Eagle* in the background
Presidential speech writer [William Safire](#40th_anniversary "Contents") had prepared an *In
Event of Moon Disaster* announcement for Nixon to read in the event the Apollo 11
astronauts were stranded on the Moon.[[167]](#Films_and_documentaries "Contents")
The remarks were in a memo from Safire to Nixon's [White House Chief of Staff](#Films_and_documentaries "Contents") [H. R. Haldeman](#See_also "Contents"), in which Safire suggested a protocol the administration might follow in reaction to such a
disaster.[[168]](#References "Contents")[[169]](#Notes "Contents") According to
the plan, Mission Control would "close down communications" with the LM, and a clergyman
would "commend their souls to the deepest of the deep" in a public ritual likened
to [burial at sea](#Citations "Contents"). The last line of the prepared text contained an allusion to [Rupert Brooke](#Sources "Contents")'s World War I poem "[The Soldier](#Sources
"Contents")".[[169]](#External_links "Contents") The script for the speech does
not make reference to Collins; as he remained onboard *[Columbia](#Multimedia "Contents")*
in orbit around the Moon, it was expected that he would be able to return the module
to Earth in the event of a mission failure.[[170]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Contents")

While moving inside the cabin, Aldrin accidentally damaged the [circuit breaker](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Contents") that would arm the main engine for liftoff from the Moon. There was a concern this would prevent firing the engine, stranding them on the Moon. The nonconductive tip of a Duro [felt-tip pen](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "vector-dropdown-checkbox
")[[171]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "vector-unpinned-container") was
sufficient to activate the switch.[[166]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "p-lang-btn")

After more than 21+1⁄2 hours on the lunar surface, in addition to the scientific
instruments, the astronauts left behind: an [Apollo 1](am "አፖሎ ፲፩ – Amharic") mission patch in memory of
astronauts [Roger Chaffee](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Aragonese"), [Gus Grissom](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Aragonese"), and [Edward White](an "Apollo 11"), who died when their command module caught fire during a test in January 1967; two memorial medals of Soviet cosmonauts [Vladimir Komarov](ar "أبولو 11 – Arabic") and [Yuri Gagarin](https://as.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%AA%27%E0%A6%B2%27_%E0%A7%A7%E0%A7%A7 "এপ'ল' ১১ – Assamese"), who died in 1967 and 1968 respectively; a memorial bag containing a gold replica of an olive branch as a traditional symbol of peace; and a silicon message disk carrying the [goodwill statements](as "এপ'ল' ১১ – Assamese") by presidents Eisenhower, Kennedy, Johnson, and Nixon along with messages from leaders of 73 countries around the
world.[[172]](https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollon_11 "Apollon 11 – Azerbaijani")
The disk also carries a listing of the leadership of the US Congress, a listing of
members of the four committees of the House and Senate responsible for the NASA legislation,
and the names of NASA's past and then-current top management.[[173]](https://ban.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Balinese")
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Апалён-11 – Belarusian (Taraškievica orthography)")](https://be-tarask.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D1%91%D0%BD-11 "Apollo 11")
A map of the [Tranquility Base](be "Апалон-11") landing site and photos taken
After about seven hours of rest, the crew was awakened by Houston to prepare for
the return flight.At that time, unknown to them, some hundred kilometers away from
them the Soviet probe [Luna 15](bg "Аполо 11") was about to descend and impact. Despite having been known to be orbiting the Moon at the same time, through a ground-breaking precautious goodwill exchange of data, the mission control of Luna 15 unexpectedly hastened its robotic [sample-return mission](bn "অ্যাপোলো ১১ – Bangla"), initiating descent, in an attempt to return before Apollo
11.[[174]](https://bs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Bosnian") Just
two hours before Apollo 11's launch, Luna 15 crashed at 15:50 UTC, with British astronomers
monitoring Luna 15 and recording the situation one commented: "I say, this has really
been drama of the highest order",[[175]](https://ceb.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_XI "Apollo XI – Cebuano")
bringing the [Space Race](ceb "Apollo XI") to a culmination.[[176]](ckb "ئەپۆلۆ ١١")

Roughly two hours later, at 17:54:00 UTC, the Apollo 11 crew on the surface safely
lifted off in *Eagle*'s ascent stage to rejoin Collins aboard *Columbia* in lunar
orbit.[[146]](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – German") Film
taken from the LM ascent stage upon liftoff from the Moon reveals the American flag,
planted some 25 feet (8 m) from the descent stage, whipping violently in the
exhaust of the ascent stage engine. Aldrin looked up in time to witness the flag
topple: "The ascent stage of the LM separated ... I was concentrating on the
computers, and Neil was studying the [attitude indicator](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apolo_11 "featured article"), but I looked up long enough to see the flag fall
over."[[177]](https://fa.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A2%D9%BE%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88_%DB%B1%DB%B1 "آپولو ۱۱ – Persian")
Subsequent Apollo missions planted their flags farther from the LM.[[178]](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – French")


### *Columbia* in lunar orbit

During his day flying solo around the Moon, Collins never felt lonely. Although it
has been said "not since [Adam](https://fy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Western Frisian") has any human known such
solitude",[[179]](https://gu.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%AA%8F%E0%AA%AA%E0%AB%8B%E0%AA%B2%E0%AB%8B_%E0%AB%A7%E0%AB%A7 "એપોલો ૧૧ – Gujarati")
Collins felt very much a part of the mission. In his autobiography he wrote: "this
venture has been structured for three men, and I consider my third to be as necessary
as either of the other two".[[179]](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%90%D7%A4%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%95_11 "אפולו 11 – Hebrew")
In the 48 minutes of each orbit when he was out of radio contact with the Earth while
*Columbia* passed round the far side of the Moon, the feeling he reported was not
fear or loneliness, but rather "awareness, anticipation, satisfaction, confidence,
almost exultation".[[179]](hu "Apollo–11")

One of Collins' first tasks was to identify the Lunar Module on the ground. To give
Collins an idea where to look, Mission Control radioed that they believed the Lunar
Module landed about 4 miles (6.4 km) off target. Each time he passed over the
suspected lunar landing site, he tried in vain to find the module. On his first orbits
on the back side of the Moon, Collins performed maintenance activities such as dumping
excess water produced by the [fuel cells](https://is.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tungllendingin_(1969) "Tungllendingin (1969) – Icelandic") and preparing the cabin for Armstrong and Aldrin to
return.[[180]](ja "アポロ11号")

Just before he reached the dark side on the third orbit, Mission Control informed
Collins there was a problem with the temperature of the coolant. If it became too
cold, parts of *Columbia* might freeze. Mission Control advised him to assume manual
control and implement Environmental Control System Malfunction Procedure 17. Instead,
Collins flicked the switch on the system from automatic to manual and back to automatic
again, and carried on with normal housekeeping chores, while keeping an eye on the
temperature.[[181]](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%95%84%ED%8F%B4%EB%A1%9C_11%ED%98%B8 "아폴로 11호 – Korean")

When *Columbia* came back around to the near side of the Moon again, Collins was
able to report that the problem had been resolved. For the next couple of orbits,
he described his time on the back side of the Moon as "relaxing". After Aldrin and
Armstrong completed their EVA, Collins slept so he could be rested for the rendezvous.
While the flight plan called for *Eagle* to meet up with *Columbia*, Collins was
prepared for a contingency in which he would fly *Columbia* down to meet *Eagle*.[[181]](lmo "Apollo XI – Lombard")


### Return
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Apollo 11 – Latvian")](https://lv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latvian")
[*Eagle*](https://mk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Apollo 11")'s
ascent stage approaching [*Columbia*](https://ml.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%B4%85%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8D%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8B%E0%B4%B3%E0%B5%8B_11 "അപ്പോളോ 11 – Malayalam")
*Eagle* rendezvoused with *Columbia* at 21:24 UTC on July 21, and the two docked
at 21:35. *Eagle*'s ascent stage was jettisoned into lunar orbit at 23:41.[[9]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
Just before the [Apollo 12](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles") flight, it was noted that
*Eagle* was still likely to be orbiting the Moon. Later NASA reports mentioned that
*Eagle*'s orbit had decayed, resulting in it impacting in an "uncertain location"
on the lunar surface.[[182]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
In 2021, however, some calculations show that the lander may still be in orbit.[[183]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

On July 23, the last night before splashdown, the three astronauts made a television
broadcast in which Collins commented: "All this is possible only through the blood,
sweat, and tears of a number of people ... All you see is the three of us, but
beneath the surface are thousands and thousands of others, and to all of those, I
would like to say, 'Thank you very much'."[[184]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Aldrin added: "This has been far more than three men on a mission to the Moon; more,
still, than the efforts of a government and industry team; more, even, than the efforts
of one nation. We feel that this stands as a symbol of the insatiable curiosity of
all mankind to explore the unknown ..."[[184]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

Armstrong concluded:

> The responsibility for this flight lies first with history and with the giants
of science who have preceded this effort; next with the American people, who have,
through their will, indicated their desire; next with four administrations and their
Congresses, for implementing that will; and then, with the agency and industry teams
that built our spacecraft, the Saturn, the Columbia, the Eagle, and the little [EMU](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), the spacesuit and backpack that was our small spacecraft out on the lunar surface. We would like to give special thanks to all those Americans who built the spacecraft; who did the construction, design, the tests, and put their hearts and all their abilities into those craft. To those people tonight, we give a special thank you, and to all the other people that are listening and watching tonight, God bless you. Good night from Apollo
11.[[184]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")


On the return to Earth, a bearing at the Guam tracking station failed, potentially
preventing communication on the last segment of the Earth return. A regular repair
was not possible in the available time but the station director, Charles Force, had
his ten-year-old son Greg use his small hands to reach into the housing and pack
it with grease. Greg was later thanked by Armstrong.[[185]](//upload.wikimedia.org "Wikipedia (en)")


### Splashdown and quarantine
[![application/atom+xml](/static/images/icons/enwiki-25.svg "Wikipedia Atom feed")](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/deed.en "Wikipedia Atom feed")
*Columbia* floats on the ocean as Navy divers assist in retrieving the astronauts.
The [aircraft carrier](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu") [USS *Hornet*](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu"), under the command of [Captain](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") [Carl J. Seiberlich](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page
[z]"),[[186]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") was selected as the primary
recovery ship (PRS) for Apollo 11 on June 5, replacing her sister ship, the [LPH](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")
[USS *Princeton*](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), which had recovered Apollo 10 on May 26.
*Hornet* was then at her home port of [Long Beach, California](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contact_us "Learn about Wikipedia and how it
works").[[187]](/wiki/Special:RecentChanges "The hub for editors") On reaching [Pearl Harbor](/wiki/Wikipedia:File_upload_wizard "Add images or other media for use on Wikipedia") on July 5,
*Hornet* [embarked](/wiki/Special:SpecialPages "A list of all special pages [q]") the [Sikorsky SH-3 Sea King](/wiki/Main_Page "A list of all special pages [q]") helicopters of [HS-4](/wiki/Main_Page "Search Wikipedia [f]"), a unit which specialized in recovery of Apollo spacecraft, specialized divers of [UDT](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]") Detachment Apollo, a 35-man NASA recovery team, and about 120 media representatives. To make room, most of
*Hornet*'s air wing was left behind in Long Beach. Special recovery equipment was
also loaded, including a [boilerplate](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]") command module used for
training.[[188]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Special:Search")

On July 12, with Apollo 11 still on the launch pad, *Hornet* departed Pearl Harbor
for the recovery area in the central Pacific,[[189]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
in the vicinity of [10°36′N 172°24′E﻿ / ﻿10.600°N 172.400°E﻿ / 10.600;
172.400](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=").[[190]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu")
A presidential party consisting of Nixon, Borman, Secretary of State [William P. Rogers](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") and [National Security Advisor](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") [Henry Kissinger](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") flew to [Johnston Atoll](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") on [Air Force One](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title="), then to the [command ship](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") [USS
*Arlington*](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=") in [Marine One](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="). After a night on board, they would fly to
*Hornet* in Marine One for a few hours of ceremonies. On arrival aboard *Hornet*,
the party was greeted by the [Commander-in-Chief, Pacific Command (CINCPAC)](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), [Admiral](# "Contents") [John S. McCain Jr.](# "Contents"), and [NASA Administrator](# "Contents") [Thomas O. Paine](# "Contents"), who flew to
*Hornet* from [Pago Pago](# "Contents") in one of *Hornet*'s [carrier onboard delivery](# "Contents")
aircraft.[[191]](#Background "Contents")

Weather satellites were not yet common, but US Air Force [Captain](#Personnel "Contents") Hank Brandli had access to top-secret [spy satellite](#Prime_crew "Contents") images. He realized that a storm front was headed for the Apollo recovery area. Poor visibility which could make locating the capsule difficult, and strong upper-level winds which "would have ripped their parachutes to shreds" according to Brandli, posed a serious threat to the safety of the
mission.[[192]](#Backup_crew "Contents") Brandli alerted Navy Captain Willard S.
Houston Jr., the commander of the [Fleet Weather Center](#Support_crew "Contents") at Pearl Harbor, who had the required security clearance. On their recommendation, [Rear Admiral](#Capsule_communicators "Contents") [Donald C. Davis](#Capsule_communicators "Contents"), commander of Manned Spaceflight Recovery Forces, Pacific, advised NASA to change the recovery area, each man risking his career. A new location was selected
215 nautical miles (398 km) northeast.[[193]](#Preparations "Contents")[[194]](#Call_signs "Contents")

This altered the flight plan. A different sequence of computer programs was used,
one never before attempted. In a conventional entry, trajectory event P64 was followed
by P67. For a skip-out re-entry, P65 and P66 were employed to handle the exit and
entry parts of the skip. In this case, because they were extending the re-entry but
not actually skipping out, P66 was not invoked and instead, P65 led directly to P67.
The crew were also warned they would not be in a full-lift (heads-down) attitude
when they entered P67.[[193]](#Pre-launch "Contents") The first program's acceleration
subjected the astronauts to 6.5 standard gravities (64 m/s2); the second, to
6.0 standard gravities (59 m/s2).[[195]](#Lunar_surface_operations "Contents")

Before dawn on July 24, *Hornet* launched four Sea King helicopters and three [Grumman E-1 Tracers](#Lunar_ascent "Contents"). Two of the E-1s were designated as "air boss" while the third acted as a communications relay aircraft. Two of the Sea Kings carried divers and recovery equipment. The third carried photographic equipment, and the fourth carried the decontamination swimmer and the flight
surgeon.[[196]](#Splashdown_and_quarantine "Contents") At 16:44 UTC (05:44 local
time) *Columbia*'s [drogue parachutes](#World_tour "Contents") were deployed. This was observed by the helicopters. Seven minutes later
*Columbia* struck the water forcefully 2,660 km (1,440 nmi) east of [Wake Island](#Cultural_significance "Contents"),
380 km (210 nmi) south of Johnston Atoll, and 24 km (13 nmi)
from *Hornet*,[[9]](#Lunar_Module_Eagle_memorabilia "Contents")[[193]](#Anniversary_events "Contents")
at [13°19′N 169°9′W﻿ / ﻿13.317°N 169.150°W﻿ / 13.317; -169.150](#See_also
"Contents").[[197]](#Sources "Contents") 82 °F (28 °C) with 6 feet (1.8 m)
seas and winds at 17 knots (31 km/h; 20 mph) from the east were reported
under broken clouds at 1,500 feet (460 m) with visibility of 10 nautical miles
(19 km; 12 mi) at the recovery site.[[198]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans")
Reconnaissance aircraft flying to the original splashdown location reported the conditions
Brandli and Houston had predicted.[[199]](am "አፖሎ ፲፩ – Amharic")

During [splashdown](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Aragonese"), *Columbia*
landed upside down but was righted within ten minutes by flotation bags activated
by the astronauts.[[200]](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Asturian")
A diver from the Navy helicopter hovering above attached a [sea anchor](https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollon_11 "Apollo 11") to prevent it from
drifting.[[201]](https://ban.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Balinese")
More divers attached flotation collars to stabilize the module and positioned rafts
for astronaut extraction.[[202]](https://bg.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 – Bulgarian")

[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Apollo 11 – German")](https://da.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Danish")

Crew of Apollo 11 in [quarantine](eo "Apollo 11") after returning to Earth, visited by Richard Nixon

[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Apollo 11 – Estonian")](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apolo_11 "Apolo 11 – Spanish")

Apollo 11 Mobile Quarantine Facility on display at the [Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center](https://fi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Finnish") in [Virginia](fi "Apollo 11 – Finnish") in 2009
The divers then passed biological isolation garments (BIGs) to the astronauts, and
assisted them into the life raft. The possibility of bringing back [pathogens](https://fy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article") from the lunar surface was considered remote, but NASA took precautions at the recovery site. The astronauts were rubbed down with a [sodium hypochlorite](fy "Apollo 11 – Western Frisian") solution and
*Columbia* wiped with [povidone-iodine](https://ga.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Irish") to remove any lunar dust that might be present. The astronauts were winched on board the recovery helicopter. BIGs were worn until they reached isolation facilities on board
*Hornet*. The raft containing decontamination materials was intentionally sunk.[[200]](gv "Apollo 11 – Manx")

After touchdown on *Hornet* at 17:53 UTC, the helicopter was lowered by the elevator
into the hangar bay, where the astronauts walked the 30 feet (9.1 m) to the
[mobile quarantine facility](https://hi.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8B_%E0%A5%A7%E0%A5%A7 "अपोलो ११ – Hindi") (MQF), where they would begin the Earth-based portion of their 21 days of
quarantine.[[203]](https://hy.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D4%B1%D5%BA%D5%B8%D5%AC%D5%B8%D5%B6_11 "Ապոլոն 11 – Armenian")
This practice would continue for two more Apollo missions, Apollo 12 and [Apollo 14](https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Indonesian"), before the Moon was proven to be barren of life, and the quarantine process
dropped.[[204]](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article")[[205]](ja "アポロ11号 – Japanese")
Nixon welcomed the astronauts back to Earth. He told them: "[A]s a result of what
you've done, the world has never been closer together before."[[206]](https://ka.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%83%90%E1%83%9E%E1%83%9D%E1%83%9A%E1%83%9D_11 "აპოლო 11 – Georgian")

After Nixon departed, *Hornet* was brought alongside the 5-short-ton (4.5 t)
*Columbia*, which was lifted aboard by the ship's crane, placed on a [dolly](kn "ಅಪೋಲೊ ೧೧ – Kannada") and moved next to the MQF. It was then attached to the MQF with a flexible
tunnel,[[207]](https://ku.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Kurdish")
allowing the lunar samples, film, data tapes and other items to be removed by MQF
project engineer [John Hirasaki](https://la.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latin"). He placed the two [Apollo Lunar Sample Return Containers](https://lmo.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_XI "Apollo XI – Lombard") (ALSRC) containing lunar samples, space suits and film cassettes into plastic bags. Hirasaki then passed the bags out of the MQF through a transfer lock with a decontamination wash. All of the collected materials were flown to [Ellington Air Force Base](https://lt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Lithuanian") in Houston and taken to the [Lunar Receiving Laboratory](https://lv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Latvian") (LRL) within 48 hours of
splashdown.[[208]](https://mg.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Malagasy")

*Hornet* returned to Pearl Harbor on July 26, where it was welcomed by thousands
of people. The MQF was loaded onto a [Lockheed C-141 Starlifter](https://min.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Minangkabau") at [Hickam Air Force Base](https://mk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 – Macedonian") and airlifted to Houston, landing on July
27.[[209]](https://ml.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%B4%85%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8D%E0%B4%AA%E0%B5%8B%E0%B4%B3%E0%B5%8B_11 "അപ്പോളോ 11 – Malayalam")
The astronauts arrived at the LRL at 10:00 UTC on July 28. *Columbia* was taken to
[Ford Island](ml "അപ്പോളോ 11") for deactivation, and its pyrotechnics made safe. It was then taken to [Hickham Air Force Base](https://mr.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%8B_%E0%A5%A7%E0%A5%A7 "अपोलो ११ – Marathi"), from whence it was flown to Houston in a [Douglas C-133 Cargomaster](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard"), reaching the Lunar Receiving Laboratory on July
30.[[207]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")

In accordance with the [Extra-Terrestrial Exposure Law](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles"), a set of regulations promulgated by NASA on July 16 to codify its quarantine
protocol,[[210]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
the astronauts continued in quarantine. After three weeks in confinement (first in
the Apollo spacecraft, then in their trailer on *Hornet*, and finally in the Lunar
Receiving Laboratory), the astronauts were given a clean bill of health.[[211]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
On August 10, 1969, the Interagency Committee on Back Contamination met in Atlanta
and lifted the quarantine on the astronauts, on those who had joined them in quarantine
(NASA physician [William Carpentier](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") and John
Hirasaki),[[212]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
and on *Columbia* itself. Loose equipment from the spacecraft remained in isolation
until the lunar samples were released for study.[[213]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
[![application/atom+xml](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=startup&only=scripts&raw=1&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
August 13, 1969, New York City


## Celebrations

Following their return to Earth, the Apollo 11 crew received widespread international
acclaim. On August 13, 1969, astronauts [Neil Armstrong](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), [Buzz Aldrin](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), and [Michael Collins](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") were honored with ticker-tape parades in [New York City](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") and [Chicago](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), with an estimated six million people lining the
streets.[[214]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
In New York the parade started at [Bowling Green](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") going down Broadway to [City Hall](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") where Mayor [John Lindsay](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") greeted them and ended at the [United Nations headquarters](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 -
Wikipedia").[[215]](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") Broadway was
even temporarily renamed for that day to "Apollo Way". In Chicago the parade went
to [the Loop](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")[[216]](//upload.wikimedia.org "Wikipedia (en)")
and culminated at the [Chicago Civic Center](/w/rest.php/v1/search "Wikipedia (en)") where the astronauts and local officials spoke to the crowd. That evening, a state dinner was held in [Los Angeles](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/deed.en "Wikipedia Atom feed") at the [Century Plaza Hotel](/w/index.php?title=Special:RecentChanges&feed=atom "Wikipedia Atom feed") to commemorate the historic achievement. The event was attended by members of [Congress](#bodyContent "Main menu"), 44 [state governors](#bodyContent "Main menu"), [Chief Justice of the United States](#bodyContent "Main menu") [Warren E. Burger](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu") and his predecessor [Earl Warren](/wiki/Main_Page "Main menu"), as well as ambassadors from 83 nations. [President](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") [Richard Nixon](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") and [Vice President](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") [Spiro Agnew](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]") awarded each astronaut the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"), the highest civilian honor in the United
States.[[217]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")
[![](/static/images/icons/enwiki-25.svg "Visit the main page [z]")](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")
Apollo 11 Astronauts - New York City - August 13, 1969
On September 16, the astronauts addressed a joint session of [Congress](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Contact_us "How to contact Wikipedia"), where they presented two [American flags](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia")—one to the [House of Representatives](/wiki/Help:Contents "Guidance on how to use and edit Wikipedia") and one to the [Senate](/wiki/Help:Introduction "Learn how to edit Wikipedia")—that had traveled to the lunar surface aboard [Eagle](/wiki/Wikipedia:Community_portal "The hub for
editors").[[218]](/wiki/Special:SpecialPages "A list of all special pages [q]")

One of the mission flags carried aboard the flight—the [Flag of American Samoa](/wiki/Main_Page "Search Wikipedia [f]")—was later displayed at the [Jean P. Haydon Museum](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]") in [Pago Pago](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]"), the capital of [American Samoa](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]"), recognizing the territory's support role as a recovery staging
area.[[219]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Search Wikipedia [f]")](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")
Terrazzo tribute to Apollo 11 astronauts on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
Numerous countries and organizations honored the Moon landing by issuing special
commemorative items. These included postage stamps, coins, medals, plaques, and magazine
features. *[TIME](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and
color")*, *[National Geographic](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and
color")*, *[LIFE](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and
color")*, and dozens of international publications featured the astronauts on their
covers. Many of these commemoratives are now held in public and private collections,
and some were placed aboard later Apollo missions in symbolic tribute.[[220]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")

Additionally, the success of Apollo 11 contributed to a brief spike in interest in
science and technology education, often referred to as the "Apollo effect", influencing
a generation of engineers and scientists.[[221]](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=")


### World tour

The celebrations continued with a 38-day world goodwill tour titled "Giant Leap",
which began on September 29 and concluded on November 5, 1969. The astronauts visited
22 countries and met with numerous heads of state, prime ministers, royalty, and
civic leaders.[[222]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options")
The tour, intended to thank the international community for their support of the
space program, began in [Mexico City](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") and ended in [Tokyo](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User
menu").[[223]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")
Notable stops included [Bogotá](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), [Buenos Aires](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), [Rio de Janeiro](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), [Madrid](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 "You are encouraged to create an account and log in; however, it is not mandatory"), [Paris](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), [Amsterdam](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), [Brussels](/w/index.php?title=Special:UserLogin&returnto=Apollo+11 " title="), [London](# "You're encouraged to log in; however, it's not mandatory.
[o]"),[[224]](# "Contents") [West Berlin](# "Contents"),[[225]](# "Contents") [Rome](# "Contents"), [Belgrade](# "Contents"), [Tehran](# "Contents"), [Mumbai](# "Contents"), [Bangkok](# "Contents"), [Sydney](# "Contents"), [Guam](# "Contents"), and [Honolulu](#
"Contents").[[224]](#Personnel "Contents") Crowds in the tens or hundreds of thousands
gathered to greet the astronauts in each city.

In London the astronauts went to [Buckingham Palace](#Prime_crew "Contents"), where they were greeted by Queen [Elizabeth II](#Prime_crew "Contents"). When they went to [West Berlin](#Prime_crew "Contents"), they were given a tour of the [Berlin Wall](#Prime_crew "Contents") by the city's mayor. In Belgrade they were greeted by a crowd of between 400,000 and 500,000 people from the airport to the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, where they placed a wreath and were welcomed to a luncheon by [Josip Broz Tito](#Backup_crew "Contents"). In [Kinshasa](#Support_crew "Contents"), Democratic Republic of the Congo, they received the [National Order of the Leopard](#Support_crew "Contents") by President [Mobutu Sese Seko](#Capsule_communicators
"Contents").[[226]](#Flight_directors "Contents")


## Legacy


### Cultural significance

Main article: [Apollo 11 in popular culture](#Insignia "Contents")[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Insignia "Contents")
A girl holding *[The Washington Post](#Site_selection "Contents")* newspaper stating
"'The Eagle Has Landed' – Two Men Walk on the Moon"
Humans walking on the Moon and returning safely to Earth accomplished Kennedy's goal
set eight years earlier. In Mission Control during the Apollo 11 landing, Kennedy's
speech flashed on the screen, followed by the words "TASK ACCOMPLISHED, July 1969".[[227]](#Mission "Contents")
The success of Apollo 11 demonstrated the United States' technological superiority;[[227]](#Launch_and_flight_to_lunar_orbit "Contents")
and with the success of Apollo 11, America had won the [Space Race](#Lunar_descent
"Contents").[[228]](#Lunar_surface_operations "Contents")[[229]](#Return "Contents")

New phrases permeated into the English language. "If they can send a man to the Moon,
why can't they ...?" became a common saying following Apollo 11.[[230]](#Celebrations "Contents")
Armstrong's words on the lunar surface also spun off various parodies.[[228]](#Legacy "Contents")

While most people celebrated the accomplishment, disenfranchised Americans saw it
as a symbol of the divide in America, evidenced by protesters led by [Ralph Abernathy](#Cultural_significance "Contents") outside of Kennedy Space Center the day before Apollo 11
launched.[[231]](#Moon_rocks "Contents") NASA Administrator [Thomas Paine](#Experiment_results "Contents") met with Abernathy at the occasion, both hoping that the space program can spur progress also in other regards, such as poverty in the US. Paine was then asked, and agreed, to host protesters as spectators at the launch, and Abernathy, awestruck by the
spectacle,[[105]](#Anniversary_events "Contents") prayed for the astronauts.[[232]](#50th_anniversary
"Contents")[*[better source needed](#See_also "Contents")*] [Jazz poet](#References "Contents") [Gil Scott-Heron](#Notes "Contents") wrote a poem called "[Whitey on the Moon](#Notes "Contents")" (1970) expressing his view that the mission was emblematic of [racial inequality in the United States](#Notes
"Contents").[[228]](#External_links "Contents") The poem starts with:

> A rat done bit my sister Nell.  

> (with Whitey on the moon)  

> Her face and arms began to swell.  

> (and Whitey's on the moon)  

> I can't pay no doctor bill.  

> (but Whitey's on the moon)  

> Ten years from now I'll be paying still.  

> (while Whitey's on the moon)  

> [...]

Twenty percent of the world's population watched humans walk on the Moon for the
first time.[[233]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "p-lang-btn") While Apollo
11 sparked the interest of the world, the follow-on Apollo missions did not hold
the interest of the nation.[[227]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans")
One possible explanation was the shift in complexity. Landing someone on the Moon
was an easy goal to understand; lunar geology was too abstract for the average person.
Another is that Kennedy's goal of landing humans on the Moon had already been accomplished.[[234]](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Aragonese")
A well-defined objective helped Project Apollo accomplish its goal, but after it
was completed it was hard to justify continuing the lunar missions.[[235]](https://as.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%8F%E0%A6%AA%27%E0%A6%B2%27_%E0%A7%A7%E0%A7%A7 "এপ'ল' ১১ –
Assamese")[[236]](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Asturian")

While most Americans were proud of their nation's achievements in space exploration,
only once during the late 1960s did the [Gallup Poll](https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollon_11 "Apollon 11 – Azerbaijani") indicate that a majority of Americans favored "doing more" in space as opposed to "doing less". By 1973, 59 percent of those polled favored cutting spending on space exploration. The Space Race had been won, and Cold War tensions were easing as the US and Soviet Union entered the era of [détente](https://azb.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A2%D9%BE%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88_11 "آپولو 11 – South Azerbaijani"). This was also a time when inflation was rising, which put pressure on the government to reduce spending. The space program was saved due to the perception that it was one of the few government programs that had achieved something great. Drastic cuts, warned [Caspar Weinberger](https://ban.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Balinese"), the deputy director of the [Office of Management and Budget](ban "Apollo 11"), might send a signal that "our best years are behind
us".[[237]](https://bg.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BE_11 "Аполо 11 – Bulgarian")

After the Apollo 11 mission, officials from the Soviet Union said landing humans
on the Moon was dangerous and unnecessary. At the time the Soviet Union was attempting
to retrieve lunar samples robotically. The Soviets publicly denied there was a race
to the Moon, and indicated they were not making an attempt.[[238]](https://bs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Bosnian")
[Mstislav Keldysh](https://ca.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Catalan") said in July 1969, "We are concentrating wholly on the creation of large satellite systems." It was revealed in 1989 that the Soviets had tried to send people to the Moon, but were unable due to technological
difficulties.[[239]](https://ckb.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A6%DB%95%D9%BE%DB%86%D9%84%DB%86_%D9%A1%D9%A1 "ئەپۆلۆ ١١ – Central Kurdish")
The public's reaction in the Soviet Union was mixed. The Soviet government limited
the release of information about the lunar landing, which affected the reaction.
A portion of the populace did not give it any attention, and another portion was
angered by it.[[240]](https://cv.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD-11 "Apollo 11")


### Spacecraft
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Apollo 11 – Welsh")](https://cy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Welsh")
