[*Columbia*](https://el.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CE%91%CF%80%CF%8C%CE%BB%CE%BB%CF%89%CE%BD_11 "Apollo 11") on display in the Milestones of Flight exhibition hall at the [National Air and Space Museum](el "Απόλλων 11 – Greek")
The [command module *Columbia*](https://eo.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Esperanto") went on a tour of the United States, visiting 49 state capitals, the [District of Columbia](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apolo_11 "featured article"), and [Anchorage, Alaska](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apolo_11 "featured
article").[[241]](https://et.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Estonian")
In 1971, it was transferred to the [Smithsonian Institution](https://eu.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Basque"), and was displayed at the [National Air and Space Museum](eu "Apollo 11 – Basque") (NASM) in Washington,
DC.[[242]](https://fi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Finnish") It was
in the central *Milestones of Flight* exhibition hall in front of the Jefferson Drive
entrance, sharing the main hall with other pioneering flight vehicles such as the
*[Wright Flyer](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – French")*,
*[Spirit of St. Louis](fr "Apollo 11 – French")*, [Bell X-1](https://fy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article"), [North American X-15](https://fy.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "good article") and *[Friendship 7](fy "Apollo
11")*.[[243]](https://gl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Galician")

*Columbia* was moved in 2017 to the NASM Mary Baker Engen Restoration Hangar at the
[Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center](https://gu.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%AA%8F%E0%AA%AA%E0%AB%8B%E0%AA%B2%E0%AB%8B_%E0%AB%A7%E0%AB%A7 "એપોલો ૧૧ – Gujarati") in Chantilly, Virginia, to be readied for a four-city tour titled
*Destination Moon: The Apollo 11 Mission*. This included [Space Center Houston](gu "એપોલો ૧૧") from October 14, 2017, to March 18, 2018, the [Saint Louis Science Center](https://gv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Manx") from April 14 to September 3, 2018, the Senator John [Heinz History Center](https://ha.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Hausa") in [Pittsburgh](https://ha.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Hausa") from September 29, 2018, to February 18, 2019, and its last location at [Museum of Flight](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%90%D7%A4%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%95_11 "אפולו 11 – Hebrew") in [Seattle](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%90%D7%A4%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%95_11 "אפולו 11 – Hebrew") from March 16 to September 2,
2019.[[242]](hi "अपोलो ११ – Hindi")[[244]](https://hu.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo%E2%80%9311 "featured article")
Continued renovations at the Smithsonian allowed time for an additional stop for
the capsule, and it was moved to the [Cincinnati Museum Center](hu "Apollo–11 – Hungarian"). The ribbon cutting ceremony was on September 29,
2019.[[245]](https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Indonesian")

For 40 years Armstrong's and Aldrin's space suits were displayed in the museum's
*Apollo to the Moon* exhibit,[[246]](io "Apollo 11") until it permanently closed
on December 3, 2018, to be replaced by a new gallery which was scheduled to open
in 2022. A special display of Armstrong's suit was unveiled for the 50th anniversary
of Apollo 11 in July 2019.[[247]](it "Apollo 11 – Italian")[[248]](https://jv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "アポロ11号")
The quarantine trailer, the flotation collar and the flotation bags are in the Smithsonian's
[Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center](jv "Apollo 11") annex near [Washington Dulles International Airport](https://ka.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%83%90%E1%83%9E%E1%83%9D%E1%83%9A%E1%83%9D_11 "აპოლო 11 – Georgian") in Chantilly, Virginia, where they are on display along with a test lunar
module.[[249]](kk "Аполлон 11")[[250]](kn "ಅಪೋಲೊ ೧೧")[[251]](https://ks.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A7%D9%BE%D9%88%D9%84%D9%88_%DB%B1%DB%B1 "اپولو ۱۱ – Kashmiri")
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Apollo 11 – Kurdish")](ks "اپولو ۱۱")
Armstrong's space suit on display at the [National Air and Space Museum](https://lmo.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_XI "Apollo XI – Lombard") in its new exhibit
The descent stage of the LM *Eagle* remains on the Moon. In 2009, the [Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter](https://lt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Lithuanian") (LRO) imaged the various Apollo landing sites on the surface of the Moon, for the first time with sufficient resolution to see the descent stages of the lunar modules, scientific instruments, and foot trails made by the
astronauts.[[252]](https://mg.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Malagasy")

The remains of the ascent stage are assumed to lie at an unknown location on the
lunar surface. The ascent stage, *Eagle*, was not tracked after it was jettisoned.
The lunar gravity field is sufficiently non-uniform to make low Moon orbits unstable
after a short time, leading the orbiting object to impact the surface.[[253]](mk "Аполо 11 – Macedonian")
However, using a program developed by NASA, and high-resolution lunar gravity data,
a paper was published, in 2021, indicating that *Eagle* might still be in orbit as
late as 2020. Using the orbital elements published by NASA, a [Monte Carlo method](ml "അപ്പോളോ 11 – Malayalam") was used to generate parameter sets that bracket the uncertainties in these elements. All simulations, of the orbit, predicted that
*Eagle* would never impact the lunar surface.[[254]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")

They were found on the Atlantic seabed using advanced sonar

conservator discovered a serial number under the rust on one of the engines raised
from the Atlantic, which NASA confirmed was from Apollo 11.[[256]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 -

Pieces of fabric and wood from the first airplane, the 1903 *[Wright Flyer](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 -
Wikipedia")*, traveled to the Moon in Apollo 11's [Lunar Module *Eagle*](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") and are displayed at the [Wright Brothers National Memorial](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia").


### Moon rocks

The main repository for the Apollo Moon rocks is the [Lunar Sample Laboratory Facility](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") at the Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center in [Houston](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), Texas. For safekeeping, there is also a smaller collection stored at [White Sands Test Facility](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") near [Las Cruces, New Mexico](//upload.wikimedia.org "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"). Most of the rocks are stored in nitrogen to keep them free of moisture. They are handled only indirectly, using special tools. Over 100 research laboratories worldwide conduct studies of the samples; approximately 500 samples are prepared and sent to investigators every
year.[[259]](//en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=rsd "Wikipedia Atom feed")[[260]](auth.wikimedia.org "Main menu")

In November 1969, Nixon asked NASA to make up about 250 presentation [Apollo 11 lunar sample displays](#bodyContent "Main menu") for 135 nations, the fifty states of the United States and its possessions, and the United Nations. Each display included Moon dust from Apollo 11 and flags, including one of the Soviet Union, taken along by Apollo 11. The rice-sized particles were four small pieces of Moon soil weighing about
50 mg and were enveloped in a clear acrylic button about as big as a [United States half-dollar coin](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]"). This acrylic button magnified the grains of lunar dust. Nixon gave the Apollo 11 lunar sample displays as goodwill gifts in
1970.[[261]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")[[262]](/wiki/Main_Page "Visit the main page [z]")


### Experiment results

The Passive Seismic Experiment ran until the command uplink failed on August 25,
1969. The downlink failed on December 14, 1969.[[263]](/wiki/Wikipedia:About "Learn about Wikipedia and how it works")
As of 2025[[update]](/wiki/Help:Introduction "Learn how to edit Wikipedia")[Lunar Laser Ranging experiment](/wiki/Special:SpecialPages "A list of all special pages [q]") remains
operational.[[264]](/wiki/Special:Search "Search Wikipedia [f]")


### Moonwalk camera

The Hasselblad camera used during the moonwalk was thought to be lost or left on
the Moon's surface.[[265]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]")


### Lunar Module *Eagle* memorabilia

In 2015, after Armstrong died in 2012, his widow contacted the [National Air and Space Museum](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]") to inform them she had found a white cloth bag in one of Armstrong's closets. The bag contained various items, which should have been left behind in the [Lunar Module
*Eagle*](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Search Wikipedia [f]"), including the 16mm Data Acquisition Camera that had been used to capture images of the first Moon
landing.[[266]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and
color")[[267]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Change the appearance of the page's font size, width, and color")
The camera is currently on display at the National Air and Space Museum.[[268]](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=")


### Anniversary events

Further information: [Apollo 11 anniversaries](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=")


#### 40th anniversary
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Log in and more options")](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "Log in and more options")
*Columbia* at the Mary Baker Engen Restoration Hangar
On July 15, 2009, [Life.com](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en "User menu") released a photo gallery of previously unpublished photos of the astronauts taken by
*Life* photographer [Ralph Morse](https://donate.wikimedia.org/?wmf_source=donate&wmf_medium=sidebar&wmf_campaign=en.wikipedia.org&uselang=en " title=") prior to the Apollo 11
launch.[[269]](/w/index.php?title=Special:CreateAccount&returnto=Apollo+11 " title=")
From July 16 to 24, 2009, NASA streamed the original mission audio on its website
in real time 40 years to the minute after the events occurred.[[270]](# "Contents")
It is in the process of restoring the video footage and has released a preview of
key moments.[[271]](# "Contents") In July 2010, air-to-ground voice recordings and
film footage shot in Mission Control during the Apollo 11 powered descent and landing
was re-synchronized and released for the first time.[[272]](# "Contents") The [John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum](# "Contents") set up an [Adobe Flash](# "Contents") website that rebroadcasts the transmissions of Apollo 11 from launch to landing on the
Moon.[[273]](#Background "Contents")

On July 20, 2009, Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins met with President [Barack Obama](#Personnel "Contents") at the White
House.[[274]](#Prime_crew "Contents") "We expect that there is, as we speak, another
generation of kids out there who are looking up at the sky and are going to be the
next Armstrong, Collins, and Aldrin", Obama said. "We want to make sure that NASA
is going to be there for them when they want to take their journey."[[275]](#Support_crew "Contents")
On August 7, 2009, an act of Congress awarded the three astronauts a [Congressional Gold Medal](#Support_crew "Contents"), the highest civilian award in the United States. The bill was sponsored by Florida Senator [Bill Nelson](#Capsule_communicators "Contents") and Florida Representative [Alan Grayson](#Flight_directors
"Contents").[[276]](#Other_key_personnel "Contents")[[277]](#Preparations "Contents")

A group of British scientists interviewed as part of the anniversary events reflected
on the significance of the Moon landing:

> It was carried out in a technically brilliant way with risks taken ... that
would be inconceivable in the risk-averse world of today ... The Apollo programme
is arguably the greatest technical achievement of mankind to date ... nothing
since Apollo has come close [to] the excitement that was generated by those astronauts—Armstrong,
Aldrin and the 10 others who followed them.[[278]](#Mission "Contents")


#### 50th anniversary

Further information: [Apollo 11 50th Anniversary commemorative coins](#Lunar_descent "Contents")
In June 2015, Congressman [Bill Posey](#Landing "Contents") introduced resolution H.R. 2726 to the 114th session of the [United States House of Representatives](#Lunar_surface_operations "Contents") directing the [United States Mint](#Lunar_surface_operations "Contents") to design and sell commemorative coins in gold, silver and clad for the 50th anniversary of the Apollo 11 mission. On January 24, 2019, the Mint released the [Apollo 11 Fiftieth Anniversary commemorative coins](#Lunar_ascent "Contents") to the public on its
website.[[279]](#Return "Contents")[[280]](#Splashdown_and_quarantine "Contents")

A documentary film, *[Apollo 11](#Celebrations "Contents")*, with restored footage
of the 1969 event, premiered in [IMAX](#Celebrations "Contents") on March 1, 2019, and broadly in theaters on March
8.[[281]](#World_tour "Contents")[[282]](#Legacy "Contents")

The Smithsonian Institute's [National Air and Space Museum](#Legacy "Contents") and [NASA](#Cultural_significance "Contents") sponsored the "Apollo 50 Festival" on the [National Mall](#Cultural_significance "Contents") in Washington DC. The three-day (July 18 to 20, 2019) outdoor festival featured hands-on exhibits and activities, live performances, and speakers such as [Adam Savage](#Spacecraft "Contents") and NASA
scientists.[[283]](#Moon_rocks "Contents")
[![Featured article](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/e7/Cscr-featured.svg/20px-Cscr-featured.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "Contents")](#Moon_rocks "Contents")
A Saturn V rocket projected onto the [Washington Monument](#Lunar_Module_Eagle_memorabilia "Contents") during the Apollo 11 50th anniversary show
As part of the festival, a projection of the 363-foot (111 m) tall [Saturn V](#40th_anniversary "Contents") rocket was displayed on the east face of the
555-foot (169 m) tall [Washington Monument](#Films_and_documentaries "Contents") from July 16 to the 20th from
9:30 pm until 11:30 pm (EDT). The program  included a 17-minute show that
combined full-motion video projected on the Washington Monument to recreate the assembly
and launch of the [Saturn V](#See_also "Contents") rocket.[[284]](#Notes "Contents")

The projection was joined by a 40-foot (12 m) wide recreation of the [Kennedy Space Center](#Citations "Contents") countdown clock and two large video screens showing archival footage to recreate the time leading up to the moon landing. There were three shows per night on July 19–20, with the last show on Saturday, delayed slightly so the portion where Armstrong first set foot on the Moon would happen exactly 50 years to the second after the actual
event.[[284]](#Multimedia "Contents")

On July 19, 2019, the [Google Doodle](#Multimedia "Contents") paid tribute to the Apollo 11 Moon landing, complete with a link to an animated YouTube video with voiceover by astronaut [Michael Collins](#Multimedia
"Contents").[[285]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Contents")[[286]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "vector-page-titlebar-toc-checkbox")

Aldrin, Collins, and Armstrong's sons were hosted by President [Donald Trump](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "vector-unpinned-container") in the Oval
Office.[[287]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "p-lang-btn")[[288]](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans")


## Films and documentaries

- *[Footprints on the Moon](https://af.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Afrikaans")*, a 1969 documentary film by Bill Gibson and Barry Coe[[289]](https://am.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E1%8A%A0%E1%8D%96%E1%88%8E_%E1%8D%B2%E1%8D%A9 "አፖሎ ፲፩ – Amharic")
- *[Moonwalk One](am "አፖሎ ፲፩")*, a 1971 documentary film by [Theo Kamecke](https://an.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Aragonese")[[290]](ar "أبولو 11 – Arabic")
- *Apollo 11: As It Happened*, a 1994 six-hour documentary on ABC News' coverage of the event[[291]](https://ast.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Asturian")
- *[Apollo 11](https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollon_11 "Apollon 11 – Azerbaijani")*, a 1996 docudrama[[292]](https://ban.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Balinese")
- *[First Man](ban "Apollo 11")*, 2018 film by [Damien Chazelle](https://be-tarask.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D1%91%D0%BD-11 "Апалён-11 – Belarusian (Taraškievica orthography)") based on the 2005 [James R. Hansen](be-tarask "Апалён-11 – Belarusian (Taraškievica orthography)") book *[First Man: The Life of Neil A. Armstrong](https://be.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD-11 "Апалён-11")*
- *[Apollo 11](https://be.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BE%D0%BD-11 "Апалон-11 – Belarusian")*, a 2019 documentary film by Todd Douglas Miller with restored footage of the 1969 event[[293]](bg "Аполо 11")[[294]](bn "অ্যাপোলো ১১")
- *[Chasing the Moon](https://br.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Breton")*, a July 2019 [PBS](https://bs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Bosnian") three-night six-hour documentary, directed by [Robert Stone](https://bs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Bosnian"), examined the events leading up to the mission. An accompanying book of the same name was also released.[[295]](https://ceb.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_XI "Apollo XI – Cebuano")
- *8 Days: To the Moon and Back*, a PBS and [BBC Studios](https://ckb.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D8%A6%DB%95%D9%BE%DB%86%D9%84%DB%86_%D9%A1%D9%A1 "ئەپۆلۆ ١١ – Central Kurdish") 2019 documentary film by Anthony Philipson re-enacting major portions of the mission using mission audio recordings, new studio footage, NASA and news archives, and computer-generated imagery.[[296]](https://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11 – Czech")
